    "name": "Ademico Peppol REST API V2 Test",
    "description": "# Introduction\n\nThe Ademico Peppol REST API connects your ERP or business application to the Peppol network. Use it to send and receive\ninvoices, credit notes and orders, manage participants, and track document processing through notifications.\n\nStart with [Getting started](#section/Getting-started) for a walkthrough of your first document exchange.\nSee [Generating your API client](#section/Application-integration/Generating-your-API-client) to create a client library\nfor your application.\n\n> **INFO** Use the <a href=\"https://peppol-tools.ademico-software.com/\" target=\"_blank\">Peppol Tools web application</a>\n> for interactive document validation and participant lookup. To integrate these tools into your software,\n> see the <a href=\"https://ademico-software.com/peppol-tools-api/\" target=\"_blank\">Peppol Tools API reference</a>.\n\n# Environments\n\nAdemico Peppol REST API is accessible in two environments:\n\n- TEST\n- PROD\n\n## TEST environment\n\nThe TEST environment is used to perform tests with the Ademico Peppol REST API and integrate it with your ERP or\nsoftware\napplication. TEST environment is using the SMK, the Peppol TEST environment.\n\nIt is not a problem to send invoices or other documents to other participants in the Peppol network in the TEST\nenvironment, they are not legally\nbinding.\n\nThe base URL paths for our TEST environment are different depending on if you are using OAuth2 or Basic\nAuthentication:\n\n- OAuth2: `https://test-peppol-api.ademico-software.com`\n- Basic Authentication: `https://test-peppol-api1.ademico-software.com/domibus`\n\nOnce you have finished your integration in TEST environment, you can move to the PROD environment.\n\n## PROD environment\n\nPROD environment is used to send legally binding invoices/credit notes to your business partners. We recommend using the\nPROD environment after you have finished your tests in our TEST environment.\n\nThe base URL paths for our PROD environment are:\n\n- OAuth2: `https://peppol-api.ademico-software.com`\n- Basic Authentication: `https://peppol-api1.ademico-software.com/domibus`\n\n# Authentication\n\nAdemico Peppol REST API supports the following types of authentication:\n\n- OAuth2\n- Basic authentication\n\n## OAuth2\n\nAccess is granted via an OAuth2 authorization server using the client credentials grant.\n\n### Credentials required for an API request\n\nEvery OAuth2 request to the Ademico Peppol REST API uses two separate credentials:\n\n1. An **OAuth access token (JWT)** obtained from the OAuth2 token endpoint using your `client_id` and `client_secret`.\n   Send this token in the `Authorization` header.\n2. An **Ademico API access token** supplied to you by Ademico. Send this value in the `accessToken` header on\n   every API request. This token is specific to the TEST or PROD environment.\n\n> **IMPORTANT** The OAuth JWT and the `accessToken` header are different credentials and are not\n> interchangeable. Obtaining an OAuth JWT does not replace the required `accessToken` header.\n\n### Step 1: Obtain an OAuth access token\n\nUse the token endpoint for your environment:\n\n- TEST: `https://test-peppol-oauth2.ademico-software.com/oauth2/token`\n- PROD: `https://peppol-oauth2.ademico-software.com/oauth2/token`\n\nReplace `YOUR_CLIENT_ID` and `YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET` with the OAuth2 client credentials supplied to you. The following\nexample obtains a JWT in the TEST environment. The `--user` option makes curl send the client credentials using HTTP\nBasic authentication:\n\n```shell\ncurl --request POST \\\n  --user 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID:YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET' \\\n  --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \\\n  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials' \\\n  --data 'scope=peppol/document' \\\n  'https://test-peppol-oauth2.ademico-software.com/oauth2/token'\n```\n\nA successful response looks similar to:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"access_token\": \"eyJraWQiOiJ...\",\n  \"expires_in\": 3600,\n  \"token_type\": \"Bearer\"\n}\n```\n\nCopy the complete value of `access_token`. The JWT expires after approximately one hour, after which you must request a\nnew one.\n\n### Step 2: Call the Ademico Peppol REST API\n\nSend the OAuth JWT in the `Authorization` header:\n\n- `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN`\n\nAlso add the Ademico API access token to the request as the `accessToken` header. This example calls the\nconnectivity endpoint in the TEST environment using the standard `Bearer` form:\n\n```shell\ncurl --request GET \\\n  --header 'accessToken: YOUR_API_ACCESS_TOKEN' \\\n  --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN' \\\n  --header 'Accept: application/json' \\\n  'https://test-peppol-api.ademico-software.com/api/peppol/v2/tools/connectivity'\n```\n\nA successful request returns HTTP status `200`. HTTP status `401` means that one or more authentication credentials are\nmissing or invalid.\n\n## Basic Authentication\n\nWhen using Basic Authentication, you need to send in your HTTP request an `Authorization` header that contains the\nword `Basic`\nword followed by a space and a base64-encoded string username:password.\n\nFor example, to authenticate as user / mypassword you would need to\nsend `Authorization: Basic YOUR_USERNAME_AND_PASSWORD_BASE64`.\n\nIn the examples from the following chapters, you would need to replace `YOUR_USERNAME_AND_PASSWORD_BASE64`\nwith your credentials in base64-encoded format.\n\nWhen using Basic Authentication, you need to use the `accessToken` header in each request.\n\n> **NOTE** Contact us to send you the value of the `accessToken` which is specific to each environment TEST/PROD.\n\nExample of a curl request using Basic Authentication:\n\n```shell\ncurl -X GET -H \"accessToken: YOUR_API_ACCESS_TOKEN\" -H \"Authorization: Basic YOUR_USERNAME_AND_PASSWORD_BASE64\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \"https://test-peppol-api1.ademico-software.com/domibus/api/peppol/v2/tools/connectivity\"\n```\n\n<!-- ReDoc-Inject: <security-definitions> -->\n\nRequests containing an `accessToken` query parameter are rejected, even when the header is also present.\n\n# Errors\n\nUse the HTTP status and error response documented for the operation you called. An error detail contains a\n`code` and a `message`; its placement in the response depends on the operation. For example:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"code\": \"GENERIC_ERROR\",\n  \"message\": \"Details of the occurred error\"\n}\n```\n\nFor asynchronous submissions, a successful response confirms acceptance. Later delivery or reporting failures can appear\nin notifications; use [Poll unconsumed notifications](#tag/Notification/operation/getNotificationsV2) or your configured\nwebhook receiver to track them. Before repeating a submission after a timeout or uncertain response, check whether\nit was accepted. Validation and conversion responses can also contain more specific detail codes.\n\nThe groups below describe where codes commonly occur. Common errors can apply to any operation; each operation's\nreference defines its HTTP statuses and response shape.\n\n## Common errors\n\nThese errors concern authentication, request values or service availability. Use\n[Check access to our service](#tag/Connectivity/operation/testConnectivity) to check your credentials and access token.\n\n| Code | What it means | What to do |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `SECURITY_ERROR` | Authentication or credential validation failed. | Check the credentials, token expiry and required `accessToken` for the selected environment. |\n| `USER_ERROR` | Request values or access settings prevent the operation. | Correct the values named in the message; contact support if the problem concerns access settings. |\n| `CONFIGURATION_ERROR` | The service configuration prevents the operation. | Contact support with the operation and error details. |\n| `GENERIC_ERROR` | The operation failed for a reason outside the specific codes below. | Read the message and check the outcome before retrying a submission. Contact support if the problem persists. |\n\n## Legal entities and registrations\n\nRelevant operations include [Create a legal entity](#tag/Legal-Entity/operation/createLegalEntityV2),\n[Register a legal entity in the Peppol network](#tag/Legal-Entity-Peppol-Registration/operation/createPeppolRegistrationForLegalEntityV2),\n[Find France Annuaire Peppol identifiers](#tag/France-Annuaire/operation/findPeppolIdentifiersBySirenOrSiret) and\n[Search France Annuaire routing codes](#tag/France-Annuaire/operation/searchRoutingCodes).\nThese codes can reject a request. After acceptance, follow the applicable registration or deletion status and notifications.\n\n| Code | What it means | What to do |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `LEGAL_ENTITY_ERROR` | A legal-entity or registration operation could not be completed. | Check the entity and registration identifiers, current state and validation message before retrying. |\n| `FRANCE_ANNUAIRE_ERROR` | **France only:** a directory lookup, registration or routing-code operation failed. | Check the reported SIREN, SIRET or addressing details. If the outcome is uncertain, check the current state before retrying; contact support for unresolved technical failures. |\n\n## Document submission and validation\n\nThese codes can reject [Send a UBL invoice or credit note](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/submitUblFile),\n[Send a UBL order](#tag/Order/operation/submitOrderFile) and other document submissions. Read the returned validation\ndetails together with the [supported document formats](#section/Supported-Peppol-documents).\n\n| Code | What it means | What to do |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `UNKNOWN_DOCUMENT_TYPE` | The document type could not be recognized. | Use a supported document type and format with the matching submission operation. |\n| `DUPLICATE_DOCUMENT` | The document was already submitted. | Check the existing submission with [Search exchanged documents](#tag/Documents/operation/getDocumentsV2) before sending again. |\n| `SUBMITTED_DOCUMENT_NOT_VALID` | The file or document values are invalid. | Correct the reported file type, empty content or inconsistent values before resubmitting. |\n| `XML_VALIDATION_ERROR` | The content is not valid XML. | Correct the XML syntax and encoding errors identified in the validation details. |\n| `XSD_VALIDATION_ERROR` | The XML does not match its document schema. | Correct the reported elements, attributes or structure for the selected document type and version. |\n| `SCHEMATRON_VALIDATION_ERROR` | The document fails business validation rules. | Correct the reported rule violations before resubmitting. |\n| `GENERIC_VALIDATION_ERROR` | Validation failed or could not complete. | Follow the validation details; contact support if they do not identify a correction you can make. |\n| `SBDH_ERROR` | The Standard Business Document Header could not be processed. | Check the sender/receiver identifiers and any supplied SBDH identifier. Contact support if those details are correct. |\n\n## Participant lookup and delivery\n\nParticipant lookup can fail while [sending a document](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/submitUblFile).\nCheck the submission response for immediate failures and [Poll unconsumed notifications](#tag/Notification/operation/getNotificationsV2)\nor webhooks for subsequent delivery failures.\n\n| Code | What it means | What to do |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `PARTICIPANT_LOOKUP_ERROR` | The receiver's Peppol registration or supported document types could not be determined. | Check the receiver identifier and confirm that it can receive the document type. Contact support if lookup keeps failing. |\n| `DOCUMENT_TRANSMISSION_ERROR` | Delivery to the receiver failed. | Inspect the delivery details and current document status before resubmitting. Contact support if the outcome remains uncertain. |\n\n## Tax reporting\n\nRelevant operations are [Request France PPF invoice reporting](#tag/France-PPF-Submission/operation/requestFranceEInvoicingC5Reporting),\n[Submit France e-reporting XML](#tag/France-PPF-Submission/operation/submitFranceEReportingXmlForLegalEntity),\n[Submit sales to Singapore IRAS](#tag/Singapore-IRAS-Submission/operation/sendSalesToSingaporeIras) and\n[Submit purchases to Singapore IRAS](#tag/Singapore-IRAS-Submission/operation/sendPurchasesToSingaporeIras).\nErrors may be returned during submission. For asynchronous reporting, check notifications for the later outcome.\n\n| Code | What it means | What to do |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `C5_ERROR` | Reporting to the tax authority could not be completed. | Read the validation or reporting details and correct any identified issue. Check the existing reporting outcome before resubmitting; contact support if no corrective action is given. |\n\n## Document retrieval, PDF and conversion\n\nThese errors are returned by document retrieval operations, including\n[Get a readable PDF](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/getInvoiceInPdfFormat),\n[Get an invoice in UBL format](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/getInvoiceInUBLFormat),\n[Get an invoice in CII format](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/getInvoiceInCIIFormat) and\n[Get an invoice in Factur-X format](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/getInvoiceInFacturxFormat).\n\n| Code | What it means | What to do |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` | The requested document or retained content is unavailable to the caller. | Check the transmission identifier, credentials and retention period; use [Search exchanged documents](#tag/Documents/operation/getDocumentsV2) to locate the document. |\n| `PDF_INVALID_REQUEST` | The PDF options or source document are unsupported. | Check the download parameters and supported profiles before repeating the request. |\n| `PDF_RENDERING_FAILED` | PDF generation failed. | Retry the download later; contact support if it continues to fail. |\n| `CONVERSION_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` | The requested format conversion is unsupported. | Request a supported format or retrieve the retained source format. |\n| `INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | The invoice exceeds the supported conversion input size. | Retrieve the retained source format or contact support about the size limit. |\n| `OUTPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | The converted document exceeds the supported output size. | Retrieve the retained source format or contact support about the size limit. |\n| `CONVERSION_FAILED` | The invoice could not be converted. | Read the error message; contact support if it gives no correction you can make. |\n| `CONVERSION_UNAVAILABLE` | Invoice conversion is temporarily unavailable. | Retry the download later; contact support if it remains unavailable. |\n| `CONVERTER_TIMEOUT` | The invoice conversion timed out. | Retry the download later; contact support if the timeout recurs. |\n| `INVALID_CONVERTER_RESPONSE` | Invoice conversion did not produce a usable result. | Retry the download later; contact support if the problem persists. |\n\n# Supported Peppol documents\n\nYou can use the Ademico Peppol REST API to send and receive the following document types in the Peppol network.\nLinked document names open available sample files. |\n| France UBL Credit Note Extension      | FR_UBL_CREDIT_NOTE_EXTENSION_NONREGULATED | urn:cen.eu:en16931:2017#conformant#urn:peppol:france:billing:extended:1.0::2.1 |                         | urn:peppol:france:billing:non-regulated    |\n| France Factur-X                       | FR_FACTUR_X_REGULATED                    |           | urn:cen.eu:en16931:2017#conformant#urn:peppol:france:billing:Factur-X:1.0::D22B | urn:peppol:france:billing:non-regulated    |\n\nFactur-X exchange supports the EN16931 and Extended Submit the original PDF to the [Factur-X submission endpoint](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/submitFacturXFile). The PDF's XMP conformance level must match the embedded CII profile (BT-24), and the CII must include the seller and buyer routing endpoints and an applicable French billing framework (BT-23). Extended uses the same regulated/non-regulated transport identifiers shown above.\n\nThe [Factur-X download endpoint](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/getInvoiceInFacturxFormat) returns the original PDF. For submitted EN16931 and Extended documents whose sender is registered in France under Peppol scheme `0225`, with automatic PPF reporting enabled, an independent Full extraction is prepared and validated before Peppol dispatch. For Peppol exchange, use the applicable customization and process\nidentifiers in the France section of [Supported Peppol documents](#/integration-reference/formats).\n\n- <a href=\"fr/sample-invoice-ubl-fr.xml\" target=\"_blank\" download>Sample Invoice UBL FR</a>\n- <a href=\"fr/sample-invoice-cii-fr.xml\" target=\"_blank\" download>Sample Invoice CII FR</a>\n\n# Getting started\n\nIn this chapter, we will guide you step by step to send and receive `Invoices` in the Peppol network TEST environment.\nSending and receiving `Credit Notes` and `Orders` is similar.\n\n> **NOTE** Before continuing to the steps below, make sure you have already obtained from us the credentials to access\n> our API.\n\n## Checking access to our API\n\nBefore sending your first `Invoice`, you need to check that you have access to our Ademico Peppol REST API.\n\nIn order to check that you have access, you need to execute a `GET` request against our\n[connectivity service](#tag/Connectivity) using the below curl command. If you get a\nstatus `200` it means that you have access, status `401` means that your authentication credentials are not correct.\n\nYou need to adapt your credentials in the example below as described in the [Authentication](#section/Authentication)\nchapter.\n\nCURL commands (or use [Connectivity REST API](#tag/Connectivity)):\n\nOAuth2:\n\n```shell\ncurl -X GET -H \"accessToken: YOUR_API_ACCESS_TOKEN\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN\" -H \"Accept: application/json\" \"https://test-peppol-api.ademico-software.com/api/peppol/v2/tools/connectivity\"\n```\n\nBasic Authentication:\n\n```shell\ncurl -X GET -H \"accessToken: YOUR_API_ACCESS_TOKEN\" -H \"Authorization: Basic YOUR_USERNAME_AND_PASSWORD_BASE64\" -H \"Accept: application/json\" \"https://test-peppol-api1.ademico-software.com/domibus/api/peppol/v2/tools/connectivity\"\n```\n\nYou can proceed to the next step after you have a successful connection.\n\n## Register your legal entity as a participant in the Peppol network\n\n### Introduction\n\nA legal entity is an organization/company that sends and receives documents eg invoices in the Peppol network.\nIt is mandatory to [create your legal entity](#tag/Legal-Entity/operation/createLegalEntityV2) before sending or receiving\ndocuments in the Peppol network.\n\nAfter you create your legal entity you can send and receive invoices and other documents. Your organization will be also\nlisted the <a href=\"https://directory.peppol.eu/public\" target=\"_blank\">Peppol Directory</a> so that it can be\ndiscovered by other participants in the Peppol network.\n\n### Register your legal entity\n\nYou can register your organization as a participant in the Peppol network using the\nAPI [create legal entity](#tag/Legal-Entity/operation/createLegalEntityV2). Below you can find an example using Basic\nAuthentication and OAuth2:\n\nBasic Authentication:\n\n```shell\ncurl -X POST \"https://test-peppol-api1.ademico-software.com/domibus/api/peppol/v2/legal-entities\" -H \"accessToken: YOUR_API_ACCESS_TOKEN\" -H \"Authorization: Basic YOUR_USERNAME_AND_PASSWORD_BASE64\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d @- << EOF\n{\n  \"legalEntityDetails\": {\n    \"publishInPeppolDirectory\": true,\n    \"name\": \"YOUR_COMPANY_NAME\",\n    \"countryCode\": \"YOUR_COMPANY_COUNTRY_CODE\",\n    \"geographicalInformation\": \"YOUR_COMPANY_STREET_AND_NUMBER, YOUR_COMPANY_CITY\",\n    \"websiteURL\": \"YOUR_COMPANY_WEBSITE\",\n    \"contacts\": [\n      {\n        \"contactType\": \"YOUR_COMPANY_CONTACT_TYPE\",\n        \"name\": \"YOUR_COMPANY_CONTACT_NAME\",\n        \"phoneNumber\": \"YOUR_COMPANY_PHONE_NUMBER\",\n        \"email\": \"YOUR_COMPANY_EMAIL\"\n      }\n    ],\n    \"additionalInformation\": \"Our company is specialized in ...\"\n  },\n  \"peppolRegistrations\": [\n    {\n      \"peppolIdentifier\": {\n        \"scheme\": \"YOUR_PEPPOL_PARTICIPANT_SCHEME\",\n        \"identifier\": \"YOUR_PEPPOL_PARTICIPANT_IDENTIFIER\"\n      },\n      \"supportedDocuments\": [\n        \"PEPPOL_BIS_BILLING_UBL_INVOICE_V3\",\n        \"PEPPOL_BIS_BILLING_UBL_CREDIT_NOTE_V3\",\n        \"PEPPOL_MESSAGE_LEVEL_RESPONSE_TRANSACTION_3_0\",\n        \"PEPPOL_INVOICE_RESPONSE_TRANSACTION_3_0\"\n      ],\n      \"peppolRegistration\": true\n    }\n  ]\n}\nEOF\n```\n\nOAuth2:\n\n```shell\ncurl -X POST \"https://test-peppol-api.ademico-software.com/api/peppol/v2/legal-entities\"  -H \"accessToken: YOUR_API_ACCESS_TOKEN\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d @- << EOF\nSame JSON as above\nEOF\n```\n\nIf you get a status `200`, it means that you have successfully registered your legal entity as a participant in the\nPeppol network. You can now search your organization by company name in\nthe <a href=\"https://test-directory.peppol.eu/public\" target=\"_blank\">Peppol Directory</a> and it will appear in the\nsearch results.\n\nWe will explain the 2 main sections from the register legal entity request from above:\n\n1. `legalEntityDetails`\n\nThis section contains the details of your organization which will be published in\nthe <a href=\"https://test-directory.peppol.eu/public\" target=\"_blank\">Peppol Directory</a> such as:\n\n- YOUR_COMPANY_NAME: The name of your company eg Ademico Software\n- YOUR_COMPANY_COUNTRY_CODE: The country in which the legal entity is registered eg BE\n- YOUR_COMPANY_STREET_AND_NUMBER, YOUR_COMPANY_CITY: The address of the legal entity eg 204 My Street, Leuven, Belgium\n- YOUR_COMPANY_WEBSITE: The company website eg https://ademico-software.com\n- YOUR_COMPANY_CONTACT_TYPE: The company contact type eg info, support\n- YOUR_COMPANY_CONTACT_NAME: The company contact name eg John Doe\n- YOUR_COMPANY_PHONE_NUMBER: The company phone number eg +32 123456\n- YOUR_COMPANY_EMAIL: The email of your organization eg info@ademico-software.com\n\nSet the flag `publishInPeppolDirectory` to false if you don't want to publish your legal entity details in the Peppol\nDirectory. In some countries, such as Singapore, it is mandatory to publish your legal entity details in Peppol\nDirectory.\n\n2. `peppolRegistrations`\n\nThis section contains the identifier of your organization in the Peppol network(`peppolIdentifier`) and defines which\ndocuments your organization can send and receive(`supportedDocuments`). A legal entity can be registered in the Peppol\nnetwork multiple times using different identifiers. For instance a legal entity in Belgium can be registered with the\ncompany registration number 0208:0552912569 and with the Belgium VAT number\n9925:BE0552912569.\n\nDepending on the country in which your organization is registered you need to use a\nspecific participant scheme and identifier in the section `peppolIdentifier`. You can have a look in the\nsection [Participant scheme and identifier](#section/Glossary/Participant-scheme-and-identifier) for more details.\n\nThe section `supportedDocuments` defines which documents your organization can send and receive. In the example above,\nthe legal entity can send and receive the following documents:\n\n- Peppol BIS Billing UBL Invoice V3(`PEPPOL_BIS_BILLING_UBL_INVOICE_V3`)\n- Peppol BIS Billing UBL CreditNote V3(`PEPPOL_BIS_BILLING_UBL_CREDIT_NOTE_V3`)\n- BIS Invoice Response(`PEPPOL_INVOICE_RESPONSE_TRANSACTION_3_0`)\n- Peppol Message Level Response transaction 3.0(`PEPPOL_MESSAGE_LEVEL_RESPONSE_TRANSACTION_3_0`)\n\nWhen you create a Peppol registration, the API can add default capabilities such as `PEPPOL_INVOICE_RESPONSE_TRANSACTION_3_0`.\nWhen you update an existing Peppol registration, the `supportedDocuments` list is applied as sent in the request, so you\ncan remove `PEPPOL_INVOICE_RESPONSE_TRANSACTION_3_0` from the registration update payload.\n\nYou can have a look in the section [Supported Peppol documents](#section/Supported-Peppol-documents) for a full list of\nsupported documents you can send or receive.\n\nBy default, `peppolRegistration=true` publishes the participant and its receiving capabilities in the Peppol network\n(SML/SMP). Set `peppolRegistration=false` to keep a local registration for sending without enabling reception through\nthis API. The sender does not need an existing SML/SMP registration; this option also supports registration managed\nby another provider. A non-empty `supportedDocuments` list is required in both cases, and country-specific registration\nrequirements still apply.\n\n`publishInPeppolDirectory=false` only hides the public Directory listing. It does not disable reception when\n`peppolRegistration=true`. To receive Peppol response documents through this API, the participant needs the corresponding\nreceiving capabilities published in SMP. French sender-only registrations use the dedicated\n[France 0225 profile](#section/Country-Specifics/Getting-started-with-Peppol-in-France/Register-a-France-0225-identifier-for-sending-only)\nwith `peppolRegistration=true` and regulated CDAR support.\n\nYou can use the API `Legal Entity Peppol Registration` to update your Peppol registration details.\n\n## Sending Invoices\n\nAfter registering your legal entity as a participant in the Peppol network, you are now ready to send your\nfirst `Invoice`. You can download an invoice template from  <a href=\"invoice-sending.xml\" target=\"_blank\" download>\nhere</a> and save it\nas `invoice-sending.xml`. Open the `invoice-sending.xml` file in a text editor and replace the following elements:\n\n- INVOICE_ID: The unique identifier of the `Invoice`\n- YOUR_PARTICIPANT_SCHEME: eg 0208 You can find\n  in [Participant scheme and identifier](#section/Glossary/Participant-scheme-and-identifier)\n  an explanation of participant scheme and participant identifier\n- YOUR_PARTICIPANT_IDENTIFIER: eg 0552912569\n\nThe other details from the invoice starting with YOUR_COMPANY_ are optional to fill in.\n\nYou can follow a similar process for sending credit notes.You can download\nfrom <a href=\"credit-note-sending.xml\" target=\"_blank\" download>here</a> a template for a Credit Note.\n\nSend your invoice by executing the following curl command:\n\nCURL commands (or use [Invoice/Credit Note REST API](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/submitUblFile)):\n\nBasic Authentication:\n\n```shell\ncurl -X POST -H \"accessToken: YOUR_API_ACCESS_TOKEN\" -H \"Authorization: Basic YOUR_USERNAME_AND_PASSWORD_BASE64\" -F \"file=@invoice-sending.xml\" \"https://test-peppol-api1.ademico-software.com/domibus/api/peppol/v2/invoices/ubl-submissions\"\n```\n\nOAuth2:\n\n```shell\ncurl -X POST -H \"accessToken: YOUR_API_ACCESS_TOKEN\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN\" -F \"file=@invoice-sending.xml\" \"https://test-peppol-api.ademico-software.com/api/peppol/v2/invoices/ubl-submissions\"\n```\n\nHTTP status `200` confirms that your invoice was accepted for processing. Delivery is asynchronous;\nuse the sending notification to determine whether it reached the receiver's Access Point or failed.\n\nNow that you have successfully scheduled an `Invoice`, you need to know if it has been correctly received by the `Buyer`\nand if the `Buyer` has accepted or rejected it. You can receive updates when an `Invoice` status changes with the help\nof the `Invoice` notifications.\n\nIn the section [Pull notifications(polling)](#section/Application-integration/Pull-Notifications-(Polling)) or\n[Push notifications(webhooks)](#section/Application-integration/Push-Notifications-(Webhooks)) you can get more details\nhow to get notifications for sent `Invoices`.\n\nHere is sequence diagram which describes the flow of sending an `Invoice` using Pull Notifications:\n\n![Sending Invoice with Pull Notifications](http://ademico-software.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Peppol-sendInvoiceUsingPullNotifications.png)\n\nHere is sequence diagram which describes the flow of sending an `Invoice` using Push(webhook) Notifications:\n\n![Sending Invoice with Push(webhook) Notifications](http://ademico-software.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Peppol-sendInvoiceUsingPushNotifications.png)\n\n## Receiving Invoices\n\nBefore receiving `Invoices`, please make sure that you\nhave [registered your legal entity](#section/Getting-started/Register-your-legal-entity-as-a-participant-in-the-Peppol-network)\nin the Peppol\nnetwork.\n\nDuring the testing phase when you are integrating your ERP or software application with our\nAPI, it is useful to register a\nsecond participant so that you can send and receive invoices or credit notes between them.\nFor instance, you [register](#section/Getting-started/Register-your-legal-entity-as-a-participant-in-the-Peppol-network)\na legal entity as a Peppol participant with\nthe identifier `9938:LU12345678` and a second participant with identifier `9938:LU12345678_part2`.\nNow in your UBL invoice you set the sending participant in the `AccountingSupplierParty`:\n\n```xml\n\n<cac:AccountingSupplierParty>\n    <cac:Party>\n        <cbc:EndpointID schemeID=\"9938\">LU12345678</cbc:EndpointID>\n    </cac:Party>\n    ..........................\n</cac:AccountingSupplierParty>\n```\n\nand the receiver of the invoice in the `AccountingCustomerParty`:\n\n```xml\n\n<cac:AccountingCustomerParty>\n    <cac:Party>\n        <cbc:EndpointID schemeID=\"9938\">LU12345678_part2</cbc:EndpointID>\n    </cac:Party>\n    ..........................\n</cac:AccountingCustomerParty>\n```\n\nOnce you sent the above invoice, you need to call\nthe [notifications endpoint](#tag/Notification/operation/getNotificationsV2) to get\nthe receiving notification.\nThe receiving notification contains the `transmissionId` which you can use\nto [retrieve the UBL invoice](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/getInvoiceInUBLFormat).\nSee also in the next sections some examples how to get the receiving notification and how to retrieve the UBL invoice.\n\nWhen a `Seller` sends you as a `Buyer` an `Invoice`, we automatically validate the `Invoice` against the Peppol\ntechnical and\nbusiness rules before informing you that you have received an `Invoice`. We perform the following checks:\n\n- XML validation\n- XSD validation\n- Schematron validation\n\nIf one of the above validation is not passing, we inform automatically the `Seller` with the reasons of the failed\nvalidation. Technically we send an `MLR` message to the `Seller`. If the `Seller` does not support receiving an `MLR`,\nwe send an `AS4 Signal` error.<br>\nIn conclusion, the `Seller` is always informed if the `Invoice` validation is not passing and if you as a `Buyer`\ncould not process the `Invoice`.\n\nIf you receive a valid `Invoice`, you will be notified either via\n[Pull notifications(polling)](#section/Application-integration/Pull-Notifications-(Polling)) or\n[Push notifications(webhooks)](#section/Application-integration/Push-Notifications-(Webhooks))\nand you get the transmission identifier (`transmissionId`) of the received `Invoice`.<br>\nUse the `transmissionId` to download the invoice in one of the formats below. These endpoints support\n**both sent and received invoices and credit notes**, subject to your access permissions and retention period.\nEvery request requires the `accessToken` header alongside Basic authentication or OAuth2.\n\n| GET endpoint | Successful response | When conversion is needed |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| [`/api/peppol/v2/invoices/{transmissionId}/ubl`](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/getInvoiceInUBLFormat) | Invoice or CreditNote XML, `application/xml` | Converts supported CII or Factur-X content to UBL 2.1. |\n| [`/api/peppol/v2/invoices/{transmissionId}/cii`](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/getInvoiceInCIIFormat) | Original CII content, `application/xml;charset=UTF-8` | Returns 500 `CONVERSION_NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; conversion to CII is not available. |\n| [`/api/peppol/v2/invoices/{transmissionId}/facturx`](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/getInvoiceInFacturxFormat) | Original PDF, `application/pdf` | Returns 500 `CONVERSION_NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; conversion to Factur-X is not available. |\n\nOriginal UBL is returned byte-for-byte with no HTTP charset override: use its XML declaration or byte-order mark\nto determine the encoding. Converted UBL is UTF-8. Factur-X originals retain the PDF bytes and embedded attachments.\nSuccessful responses contain only the requested file, without a conversion report. Conversion leaves the stored\noriginal unchanged, and matching-original downloads remain available when conversion is unavailable.\n\nConversion currently supports the ordinary EN16931 subset. Extended, BASIC WL and known unsupported structures\nare rejected for conversion to UBL; their original downloads remain available. Successful conversion does not\nvalidate the invoice or certify compliance with invoice business rules.\n\nOnly `/ubl` accepts the optional, case-sensitive `lossPolicy` query parameter:\n\n| Value | Behaviour |\n| --- | --- |\n| `REJECT` (default when omitted) | Rejects conversion warnings. |\n| `ALLOW_WITH_WARNINGS` | Allows supported conversions with warnings; the response still contains only the XML file. |\n\nBoth values reject known unsupported profiles, structures and fatal errors. The policy does not change original\nUBL retrieval. Other values return HTTP 400.\n\nEvery successful download includes `X-ADEMICO-CONVERSION-OUTCOME: original` when no conversion was needed,\nor `X-ADEMICO-CONVERSION-OUTCOME: converted` when the response was converted to UBL. CII and Factur-X downloads\ncurrently always return `original`. Errors omit the header; do not interpret a missing header as `original`.\n\nErrors use the JSON `ApplicationMessage` response with `code` and `message`:\n\n| HTTP status | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| 400 | Invalid/unsupported content, rejected loss or invalid policy. Missing, expired or inaccessible documents retain `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`. |\n| 400 | UBL conversion processing limits exceeded: `INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` or `OUTPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. |\n| 401 | Caller authentication failed. |\n| 500 | Conversion failed: `CONVERSION_FAILED` or `INVALID_CONVERTER_RESPONSE`. |\n| 500 | UBL conversion is unavailable: `CONVERSION_UNAVAILABLE`. |\n| 500 | Conversion timed out: `CONVERTER_TIMEOUT`. |\n| 500 | `CONVERSION_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` on `/cii` or `/facturx`, after access, retention and invoice eligibility checks. |\n\nUse `ApplicationMessage.code` to distinguish temporary conversion failures from unsupported target formats;\nHTTP 500 alone does not indicate that retrying will resolve the error.\n\nBrowser clients can read the header with `response.headers.get('X-ADEMICO-CONVERSION-OUTCOME')`.\nFor an already permitted cross-origin request, the response must explicitly expose it using\n`Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-ADEMICO-CONVERSION-OUTCOME` (alongside any other exposed headers).\nSame-origin requests need no CORS exposure header. A cross-origin browser may hide the outcome header even when\nit is present on the HTTP response; verify exposure before relying on it. An exposure wildcard is insufficient\nwhen the request uses `credentials: 'include'`.\n\nCURL commands (or use [Invoice/Credit Note REST API](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/getInvoiceInUBLFormat)):\n\nBasic authentication:\n\n```shell\ncurl --fail-with-body --dump-header response-headers.txt --output invoice.xml -H \"accessToken: YOUR_API_ACCESS_TOKEN\" -H \"Authorization: Basic YOUR_USERNAME_AND_PASSWORD_BASE64\" -H \"Accept: application/xml, application/json\" \"https://test-peppol-api1.ademico-software.com/domibus/api/peppol/v2/invoices/{transmissionId}/ubl?lossPolicy=REJECT\"\n```\n\nOAuth2:\n\n```shell\ncurl --fail-with-body --dump-header response-headers.txt --output invoice.xml -H \"accessToken: YOUR_API_ACCESS_TOKEN\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN\" -H \"Accept: application/xml, application/json\" \"https://test-peppol-api.ademico-software.com/api/peppol/v2/invoices/{transmissionId}/ubl?lossPolicy=REJECT\"\n```\n\nRead the HTTP status, `Content-Type` and outcome in `response-headers.txt` before processing `invoice.xml`;\non an HTTP error, the saved body is JSON. Replace the policy with `ALLOW_WITH_WARNINGS` only when you want to permit\nsupported conversions with warnings. For an original CII or Factur-X download, select `/cii` or `/facturx`, omit\n`lossPolicy`, and use the matching output extension and `Accept` media type alongside `application/json`.\n\nExample of a received invoice:\n\n```xml\n\n<Invoice xmlns:cac=\"urn:oasis:names:specification:ubl:schema:xsd:CommonAggregateComponents-2\"\n         xmlns:cbc=\"urn:oasis:names:specification:ubl:schema:xsd:CommonBasicComponents-2\"\n         xmlns=\"urn:oasis:names:specification:ubl:schema:xsd:Invoice-2\">\n    <cbc:CustomizationID>urn:cen.eu:en16931:2017#compliant#urn:fdc:peppol.eu:2017:poacc:billing:3.0\n    </cbc:CustomizationID>\n    <cbc:ProfileID>urn:fdc:peppol.eu:2017:poacc:billing:01:1.0</cbc:ProfileID>\n    <cbc:ID>pbe000512-8</cbc:ID>\n    <cbc:IssueDate>2022-05-19</cbc:IssueDate>\n    <cbc:DueDate>2022-06-19</cbc:DueDate>\n    <cbc:InvoiceTypeCode>380</cbc:InvoiceTypeCode>\n    <cbc:DocumentCurrencyCode>EUR</cbc:DocumentCurrencyCode>\n    <cbc:AccountingCost>4025:123:4343</cbc:AccountingCost>\n Notifications](http://ademico-software.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Peppol-receiveInvoiceUsingPushNotifications.png)\n\n### Receiving invoices via email\n\nIn specific cases, it is useful to be notified by email each time you receive an `Invoice`.\n\nWe will send you an email to your functional mailbox with the following content:\n\n- email subject: the invoice identifier\n- email body: invoice identifier, sender identifier(eg company registration number, VAT), sender name,\n  sender country, receiver identifier(eg company registration number, VAT), receiver name, receiver country\n- 2 email attachments:\n    - the UBL invoice in XML format\n    - the invoice in PDF format\n\nHere is an example of the contents of the email body we will send you:\n\n```html\nDocument type: Invoice\nDocument id: pbe000512-8\nSender id: 0208:0111111111\nSender name: Seller name\nSender country: Belgium\nReceiver id: 0208:0222222222\nReceiver name: Buyer name\nReceiver country: Belgium\n```\n\nAfter receiving the `Invoice` content in UBL XML format, you as a `Buyer` must process the `Invoice` in your ERP or\nsoftware\napplication. After the\nprocessing takes place, you can optionally inform the `Seller` about the status of the `Invoice`\nby sending an [Invoice Response](#tag/Invoice-Response/operation/sendInvoiceResponse) <br>\nFor instance, you might decide to accept the `Invoice` or reject it because of a business reason eg invalid purchase\norder number.\n\nPlease check the section [Invoice Response](#tag/Invoice-Response/operation/sendInvoiceResponse) for the possible values\nyou can use to inform the `Seller` of your decision.\n\n# Application integration\n\nIn this chapter, we will see how you can integrate your ERP or software application with the Ademico Peppol REST API and\nreceive\nnotifications either using [Pull notifications(polling)](#section/Application-integration/Pull-Notifications-(Polling))\nor\n[Push notifications(webhooks)](#section/Application-integration/Push-Notifications-(Webhooks))\n\n## Migrating from V1 to V2\n\nUse this guide to upgrade an existing integration in stages. V2 makes timestamps unambiguous, identifies\nnotification models explicitly and exposes French receiving Peppol registration outcomes.\nSwitching your REST client and selecting V2 webhooks are separate actions.\n\n### Who needs to migrate?\n\n| Your integration | What to do |\n| --- | --- |\n| A new integration using the current OpenAPI document | Skip the migration steps. Use [Getting started](#section/Getting-started) and [Generating your API client](#section/Application-integration/Generating-your-API-client). |\n| An existing integration using V1 operations or receiving V1 webhooks | Migrate to the documented V2 replacements and/or webhook delivery using this guide. |\n| An integration already using V2 for every REST call and V2 webhooks if webhooks are used | No V1 migration is needed. Keep using the current reference and client-generation guidance. |\n\nCheck the actual **HTTP method and path**, and the webhook **`payloadVersion`**. The account's age or the\nSDK's name does not determine whether migration is needed. For a configured receiver,\n`GET /api/peppol/v2/settings/webhooks` shows an explicitly selected version; an omitted `payloadVersion`\nmeans delivery defaults to V1.\n\nFor a **new webhook receiver**, explicitly select `payloadVersion: V2` when configuring it, as described in\n[Selecting V2 webhook delivery](#section/Application-integration/Selecting-V2-webhook-delivery).\nA new receiver starting with V2 does not need this guide's V1/V2 overlap or rollback steps.\n\n**V1 support window:** All public V1 operations and V1 webhook payloads will retire six months after the\ncomplete V2 API becomes available in production. The availability announcement will specify both dates.\nV1 contracts and date formats remain unchanged during migration. The current reference documents\nthe V2 replacement for every public V1 operation; verify availability in your environment before switching.\n\n### Migration checklist\n\n1. **Identify the calls and notifications you use.** Compare them with the documented V2 operations and the contract changes below.\n   Keep the same environment URL and credentials. Move `accessToken` from the URL query to the HTTP header.\n   Remove the query parameter entirely: V2 rejects it even when the header is present. V1 keeps its query parameter.\n2. **Choose the migration work for your client.** If you generate an SDK or typed models from OpenAPI,\n   download the current specification and generate a separate client using the documented settings.\n   If your application sends HTTP requests and reads JSON directly, client generation is unnecessary;\n   update its request parameters, JSON mappings and notification handling instead. This distinction applies\n   in any programming language. Keep the working V1 integration and frozen specification for rollback.\n3. **Update your mappings.** Read UTC instants, preserve calendar dates, select notification models using\n   `notificationType`, replace the eight receiving models' `receivedDate` access with `notificationDate`,\n   and rename `sbdhTransmissionId` to `sbdhInstanceIdentifier` where described below. Changing only the URL is insufficient.\n4. **Verify the complete workflow in TEST.** Include unknown fields, unsupported notification types,\n   retries, acknowledgement and your application running outside UTC. Use the validation checklist below.\n5. **Switch your REST calls to their documented V2 operations.** Unchanged contracts also have V2 URLs.\n   Keep notification processing and acknowledgement coordinated during the transition.\n6. **If you use webhooks, deploy a receiver that accepts both formats before opting in.** Change only\n   `payloadVersion` unless you also intend to change the receiver settings. Monitor deliveries and retries,\n   and retain both decoders until the transition is confirmed complete.\n\n### Choose the correct OpenAPI document\n\nThe current specification includes V2 operations with changed contracts and operations that retain their\ncontract at a V2 URL. Generate from the whole published document and follow its method/path pairs.\n\n| Purpose | Specification |\n| --- | --- |\n| Current REST client | [Public `openapi.json`](openapi.json) |\n| Maintain an existing V1 REST client | [Frozen public `v1/openapi.json`](v1/openapi.json) |\n| Receive a single V2 webhook notification | [Single-webhook `openapi.json`](https://ademico-software.com/peppol-webhook-rest-api/openapi.json) |\n| Receive V2 webhook batches | [Bulk-webhook `openapi.json`](https://ademico-software.com/peppol-webhook-rest-api/bulk/openapi.json) |\n| Maintain an existing V1 receiver | [Frozen webhook `v1/openapi.json`](https://ademico-software.com/peppol-webhook-rest-api/v1/openapi.json) |\n\nBoth the [public REST root `openapi.json`](https://ademico-software.com/peppol-rest-api/openapi.json) and the\n[single-webhook root `openapi.json`](https://ademico-software.com/peppol-webhook-rest-api/openapi.json) now\nserve the current contracts. Update V1 client and receiver generation jobs to use the explicit frozen public\nand webhook `v1/openapi.json` URLs in the table. The separate webhook `bulk/openapi.json` describes V2 batches.\nHistorical root download links inside archived V1 guides can also lead to the current contract; use the\nexplicit frozen URLs when maintaining V1.\n\nSelecting **Previous version (V1)** in the documentation opens the frozen reference. Keep V1 and V2 generated\ncode separate while migrating; downloading a new specification does not update an already deployed client.\n\nFollow [Generating your API client](#section/Application-integration/Generating-your-API-client) for the\nverified OpenAPI Generator C#/Java commands and Kiota consumer checks. NSwag can generate and compile C#\nmodels, but automatic decoding of notification unions is not supported by the verified configuration.\nAccept additional JSON properties without suppressing validation of known fields. Unknown notification\ntypes and enum values require explicit handling; they are not equivalent to harmless additional properties.\n\n### SBDH identifier naming\n\nV2 uses `sbdhInstanceIdentifier` wherever the API exposes the SBDH instance identifier. Rename the former\n`sbdhTransmissionId` field in document-search results, invoice/order-family notifications, C5/IRAS notifications\nand IRAS submission receipts. The document-search query parameter changes to `sbdhInstanceIdentifier` too.\nV1 keeps `sbdhTransmissionId`; V2 does not return both names.\n\nThe value and the document it identifies do not change:\n\n- Document-search results identify the listed document; submission receipts identify the submitted document.\n- Invoice and order-family notifications identify the invoice, credit note, order, change, cancellation, response\n  or balance described by that notification. An order response's SBDH belongs to the response, not its referenced order.\n- Invoice Response notifications already use `sbdhInstanceIdentifier`: it identifies the **Invoice Response message**,\n  while their `documentId` and `transmissionId` identify the original invoice or credit note.\n- C5/IRAS notifications identify the document reported to the authority, when available. Standalone reporting can\n  omit this identifier. Submission IDs, acknowledgement IDs and `c5TransmissionId` retain their separate meanings.\n\n### Update REST calls and models\n\nFor the following method/path pairs, change the prefix from `/api/peppol/v1` to `/api/peppol/v2`.\nFor example, `GET /api/peppol/v1/notifications` becomes `GET /api/peppol/v2/notifications`.\nThe path column below is appended to that prefix; all identifiers retain their meaning. These eleven\noperations have versioned contracts; the additional URL-only aliases are described after the table.\n\n| Method | Path after the version prefix | V2 change |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| GET | `/notifications` | UTC timestamps, explicit notification models and French receiving registration outcomes. |\n| GET | `/documents` | UTC document creation timestamps; `sbdhInstanceIdentifier` replaces the `sbdhTransmissionId` query parameter and response field. |\n| GET | `/legal-entities` | UTC company and nested registration dates; registration lifecycle fields. |\n| POST | `/legal-entities` | Offset-aware `registrationDate`; the ID-only creation response is unchanged. |\n| PUT | `/legal-entities/{legalEntityId}` | Offset-aware `registrationDate`; the empty update response is unchanged. |\n| GET | `/legal-entities/{legalEntityId}/peppol-registrations` | UTC creation timestamps and registration lifecycle fields. |\n| POST | `/legal-entities/{legalEntityId}/peppol-registrations` | Registration ID plus applicable lifecycle fields. |\n| GET | `/legal-entities/{legalEntityId}/peppol-registrations/{peppolRegistrationId}/c5/corppass` | UTC initiated/signed timestamps. |\n| POST | `/invoices/{transmissionId}/cdar` | Offset-aware receipt timestamp and a date-only invoice issue date. |\n| GET | `/c5/france/ppf/e-invoicing-submissions/{transmissionId}/xml` | UTC transmission and acknowledgement timestamp headers; XML content is unchanged. |\n| GET | `/c5/france/ppf/e-reporting-submissions/{submissionId}/xml` | UTC transmission and acknowledgement timestamp headers; XML content is unchanged. |\n\nThe URL-only aliases preserve their SDK method names and existing request/response contracts.\nThey cover connectivity and document counts, UBL/CII/Factur-X/PDF/CDAR downloads, the five order-family\ndownloads, transport evidence, notification acknowledgement, webhook settings, company deletion, registration\nupdate/deletion, C5/KYC actions and Annuaire identifier lookup. For example, use\n`DELETE /api/peppol/v2/notifications/{notificationId}` for acknowledgement and\n`GET /api/peppol/v2/invoices/{transmissionId}/cdar` for CDAR XML. V1 aliases remain callable during migration\nand refer to the same records.\n\nUse `DELETE /api/peppol/v2/legal-entities/{legalEntityId}` to delete a company. It uses the same company\nID and returns the same empty successful response as V1.\n\nFor registration updates and deletions, use `PUT` or `DELETE` on\n`/api/peppol/v2/legal-entities/{legalEntityId}/peppol-registrations/{peppolRegistrationId}`.\nKeep the existing company and registration IDs and update body. Both API versions retain empty HTTP 200\nresponses for accepted deletions. French Annuaire-managed `0225` receiving deletions can remain pending until\nAnnuaire closure is confirmed and cleanup completes. Use V2 reads for `deletionStatus` and V2 notifications\nfor completion; see [Delete a Peppol registration](#tag/Legal-Entity-Peppol-Registration/operation/deletePeppolRegistrationForLegalEntity)\nand [Delete a legal entity](#tag/Legal-Entity/operation/deleteLegalEntity).\nRetry failed or interrupted whole-company deletions to resume unfinished work.\n\nFor invoice uploads, use `POST` on `/api/peppol/v2/invoices/ubl-submissions`,\n`/api/peppol/v2/invoices/cii-submissions` or `/api/peppol/v2/invoices/facturx-submissions`.\nKeep the multipart `file` field and any `X-C5-REPORTING` selection. The accepted formats,\nvalidation rules, success and error fields, and document-type values remain unchanged.\nRegenerated SDKs use `DocumentSubmissionResultROV2` and `FileSubmissionResultErrorROV2`\nwith dedicated API enums; update application references to those types where needed.\nThe operation names stay `submitUblFile`, `submitCiiFile` and `submitFacturXFile`.\nDates inside the uploaded XML or PDF keep their format's requirements; this URL change\ndoes not convert invoice issue dates to UTC timestamps. V1 uploads remain callable during migration.\n\nFor order-family uploads, use `POST` under `/api/peppol/v2` with the following paths.\nKeep the multipart `file` field; XML formats, validation rules, response fields and enum\nvalues remain unchanged. These operations reuse the same REST-owned SDK response models\ndescribed above, so only the URL and generated model references need migration.\n\n| Path after `/api/peppol/v2` | SDK operation name |\n| --- | --- |\n| `/orders/ubl-submissions` | `submitOrderFile` |\n| `/order-responses/ubl-submissions` | `submitOrderResponseFile` |\n| `/order-changes/ubl-submissions` | `submitOrderChangeFile` |\n| `/order-cancellations/ubl-submissions` | `submitOrderCancellationFile` |\n| `/sg-order-balances/ubl-submissions` | `submitSgOrderBalanceFile` |\n\nTheir V1 upload endpoints remain callable during migration. Dates inside the uploaded\nUBL retain their existing meaning and format.\n\nFor invoice responses, use `POST /api/peppol/v2/invoice-responses`. Keep the existing\nJSON fields, invoice transmission ID, response codes and clarification values.\n`effectiveDate` remains a calendar date in `yyyy-MM-dd` format, not a UTC timestamp.\nRegenerated SDKs use `InvoiceResponseROV2` and `InvoiceClarificationROV2` with\n`InvoiceClarificationTypeRO` and `InvoiceClarificationCodeRO`; the existing\n`InvoiceResponseCodeEnumRO` is shared. Success uses `DocumentSubmissionResultROV2`,\nwhile errors retain `ApplicationMessage`. The operation name stays `sendInvoiceResponse`,\nand the V1 endpoint remains callable during migration.\n\nFor Factur-X generation, use `POST /api/peppol/v2/france/facturx-generations/template`\nor `POST /api/peppol/v2/france/facturx-generations/from-cii`. The template JSON uses\n`FranceFacturXTemplateGenerationRequestROV2` with the same seller and buyer fields.\nThe CII endpoint keeps the `cii` and optional `pdf` multipart parts and the `language`\nquery parameter. Both operations still accept `FR` or `EN`, default to `FR`, and\nreturn a PDF without submitting it to Peppol. A supplied PDF remains the visual\nsource, so the requested language is ignored in that case. Template errors remain\n`ApplicationMessage`; CII validation errors use `FileSubmissionResultErrorROV2`\nwith unchanged JSON fields. SDK operation names remain `generateFromTemplate`\nand `generateFromCii`, and both V1 endpoints remain callable during migration.\n\nFor Singapore IRAS reporting, use `POST /api/peppol/v2/c5/singapore/iras/sales`\nor `POST /api/peppol/v2/c5/singapore/iras/purchases`. Keep the `file` multipart part\nand the existing optional SBDH identifier header: `X-SBDH-IDENTIFIER` for sales and\n`X-SBDH_IDENTIFIER` for purchases. Success uses `IrasSubmissionResultROV2`, with\n`sbdhInstanceIdentifier` replacing `sbdhTransmissionId`. It still identifies the document submitted to IRAS.\nOther fields are unchanged, with document-type values represented by `DocumentSubmissionTypeRO`.\nValidation errors use `FileSubmissionResultErrorROV2` with unchanged JSON fields.\nThe SDK operation names remain `sendSalesToSingaporeIras` and\n`sendPurchasesToSingaporeIras`; both V1 endpoints remain callable during migration.\n\nFor France PPF reporting, use `POST` on\n`/api/peppol/v2/c5/france/ppf/e-invoicing-submissions/{transmissionId}` to request\nreporting for an already sent invoice, or\n`/api/peppol/v2/c5/france/ppf/legal-entities/{legalEntityId}/e-reporting-submissions`\nto upload e-reporting XML. Keep the existing transmission or company ID and the\ne-reporting multipart `file` field. Success uses `C5SubmissionResultROV2`, with\nthe same six fields and receiver values represented by `C5ReceiverRO`; submission\nstatus values are unchanged. E-reporting validation errors use\n`FileSubmissionResultErrorROV2` with unchanged JSON fields. SDK operation names\nremain `requestFranceEInvoicingC5Reporting` and `submitFranceEReportingXmlForLegalEntity`.\nXML formats and validation requirements remain unchanged, and both V1 endpoints\nremain callable during migration.\n\nRouting-code management is new in V2 and does not require migration from a released V1 operation.\nUse `GET` or `POST` on `/api/peppol/v2/legal-entities/{legalEntityId}/france/annuaire/routing-codes`\nto search or create codes. Search requires the `siret` query parameter. Append\n`/{siret}/{routingIdentifier}` for `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` of one code.\nAnnuaire dates are calendar dates in `yyyy-MM-dd` format.\n\nUBL download uses `GET /api/peppol/v2/invoices/{transmissionId}/ubl` with the same optional, case-sensitive\n`lossPolicy`: `REJECT` remains the default, and `ALLOW_WITH_WARNINGS` permits supported conversions with warnings.\nOriginal XML bytes, converted output, response headers and error behavior retain their existing contracts.\n\nFollow the method/path in the published specification for each public operation.\nUpdate the changed request and response models as well as the URLs; changing a\nversion prefix alone does not migrate timestamp or notification handling.\n\nURL-only aliases retain their existing date semantics. Document-count `startDateTime` and `endDateTime`\nalready accept ISO timestamps with a timezone. Calendar-only values, including invoice-response\n`effectiveDate` and Annuaire dates, keep their calendar meaning.\n\nFor both PPF XML downloads, `X-C5-TRANSMISSION-DATE` and `X-C5-ACKNOWLEDGEMENT-DATE` change from\ntheir legacy textual representation to ISO 8601 UTC with three fractional digits and `Z`, for example\n`2026-01-15T10:11:12.123Z`. Update any custom header parser; generated clients may expose a date-time\ntype for these headers. V1 keeps its existing textual representation, which is not a single guaranteed\nISO 8601 UTC format. Both versions omit a date header when the date is unavailable. The SDK operation\nnames, XML content, other headers and identifiers remain unchanged.\n\nExisting entity, registration, document and notification identifiers remain valid. Migration does not require\nrecreating participants or resubmitting documents. V2 polling does not create an independent notification inbox:\nV1 and V2 share notification identity and acknowledgement state. Coordinate consumers so switching clients\ndoes not process the same business event twice.\n\n### Update dates and field mappings\n\nV1 JSON timestamp fields representing instants are documented as UTC without a timezone suffix;\nV2 makes that UTC meaning explicit with `Z`.\nV2 response timestamps use UTC with three fractional digits and `Z`, for example\n`2026-07-28T04:33:35.000Z`. Keep them as instants in your application and convert to local time only for display.\nRetained timestamp fields keep their names; there are no parallel `...Utc` fields to choose between.\n\n| Value | V1 example or behavior | V2 example or behavior |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| An instant such as `notificationDate` | `2026-07-28T04:33:35.000` without a timezone suffix | `2026-07-28T04:33:35.000Z` explicitly identifies UTC. |\n| PPF download `X-C5-TRANSMISSION-DATE` and `X-C5-ACKNOWLEDGEMENT-DATE` headers | Legacy textual timestamp representation | `2026-01-15T10:11:12.123Z`; the XML document's own dates keep their specified formats. |\n| Company `registrationDate` in a request | Legacy timestamp parser | Send `2026-07-28T06:33:35.123+02:00` or `2026-07-28T04:33:35.123Z`; both identify the same instant. |\n| CDAR `referencedDocument.receiptDateTime` in a request | `2026-07-28T04:33:35` | Send `2026-07-28T06:33:35.123+02:00`; the normalized UTC instant is `2026-07-28T04:33:35Z`, with fractional seconds discarded. This identifies the instant, not a response or CDAR XML representation. |\n| CDAR `referencedDocument.issueDate` | `2026-07-28T00:00:00` | `2026-07-28`; preserve the invoice's calendar date without timezone conversion. |\n| Receiving-model `receivedDate` | Receipt timestamp | For the eight models listed below, `notificationDate` preserves this instant. |\n| Registration lifecycle fields | Absent from V1 responses | V2 adds applicable `registrationStatus`, `registrationStatusMessage` and `activationDate`. |\n\nThe date examples explain the contracts; they are not instructions to append `Z` to arbitrary stored strings.\nWhen sending V2 requests, derive the instant from your application's known date/time and timezone, then serialize\nit with `Z` or an explicit offset. V2 rejects offset-less writable timestamps. Keep the documented legacy parser\nfor any timestamp-bearing responses or webhook payloads your integration still receives through V1 during migration.\n\nFor example, these are the date fields within a V2 structured CDAR request, not a complete submission:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"referencedDocument\": {\n    \"issueDate\": \"2026-07-28\",\n    \"receiptDateTime\": \"2026-07-28T06:33:35.123+02:00\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\nAn omitted or null CDAR `issueDate` uses the referenced invoice's issue date; a supplied date must match it.\nInvoice-response `effectiveDate` also remains a calendar date. Preserve null or omitted values according\nto each schema instead of inventing dates. See [Dates and time zones](#section/Application-integration/Dates-and-time-zones)\nfor the complete timestamp rules.\n\nV2 removes `receivedDate` from these eight receiving models: invoice, failed document, MLR, order,\norder change, order cancellation, advanced order response and Singapore order balance.\nFor these models, V2 `notificationDate` carries the instant previously returned in V1 `receivedDate`.\nV1 `notificationDate` can be null for the five order-receiving variants; the two V1 fields were not always identical.\nDistinct dates remain, including `acknowledgementDate`,\nregistration `activationDate` and CDAR `receiptDateTime`.\n\n### Use notificationType as the discriminator\n\n`notificationType` tells your client **which JSON model to decode**. `eventType` tells your application\n**what happened**. They serve different purposes: both an invoice and an order can have\n`eventType: \"DOCUMENT_RECEIVED\"`, but their models are `INVOICE_RECEIVING` and `ORDER_RECEIVING`.\nLikewise, the `INVOICE_SENDING` model can describe `DOCUMENT_SENT` or `DOCUMENT_SEND_FAILED`.\nDo not select a model using `eventType` alone.\n\nAt each notification location—the polling array items, a single webhook body and the items in a bulk webhook—the\nV2 OpenAPI schema uses `oneOf` for the alternative models and declares `notificationType` as its **discriminator**.\nThe discriminator mapping associates each wire value with a concrete schema, such\nas `INVOICE_RECEIVING` with `InvoiceReceivingNotificationROV2`. A supported generator uses this mapping to\nselect the model while decoding. It does not replace your business handling of `eventType`, and it does not\nguarantee that every generator handles polymorphism correctly; follow the client-generation guidance above.\n\n| `notificationType` | Concrete schema | Example `eventType` values |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `INVOICE_RECEIVING` | `InvoiceReceivingNotificationROV2` | `DOCUMENT_RECEIVED` |\n| `ORDER_RECEIVING` | `OrderReceivingNotificationROV2` | `DOCUMENT_RECEIVED` |\n| `INVOICE_SENDING` | `InvoiceSendingNotificationROV2` | `DOCUMENT_SENT`, `DOCUMENT_SEND_FAILED` |\n\nThe following responses show the same received-invoice event from one independent example scenario,\nproduced by the application with fictional business data. Each example is one notification item; polling wraps items in `notifications` alongside\n`pagination`, while a single webhook uses the item itself as its request body.\n\n**V1**\n\n```json\n{\n  \"eventType\": \"DOCUMENT_RECEIVED\",\n  \"notificationId\": 2,\n  \"notificationDate\": \"2026-10-28T17:38:47.807\",\n  \"transmissionId\": \"962f9005-9822-3299-a8be-b34da976fe88\",\n  \"sbdhTransmissionId\": \"8045bb7c-9e92-376f-adf6-2c7b3ab00c89\",\n  \"documentId\": \"INVOICE-2026-200\",\n  \"peppolDocumentType\": \"INVOICE\",\n  \"sender\": \"0208:1999999943\",\n  \"receiver\": \"0208:0552912569\",\n  \"receivedDate\": \"2026-10-28T17:38:47.807\",\n  \"details\": []\n}\n```\n\n**V2**\n\n```json\n{\n  \"eventType\": \"DOCUMENT_RECEIVED\",\n  \"notificationId\": 2,\n  \"notificationDate\": \"2026-10-28T17:38:47.807Z\",\n  \"transmissionId\": \"962f9005-9822-3299-a8be-b34da976fe88\",\n  \"sbdhInstanceIdentifier\": \"8045bb7c-9e92-376f-adf6-2c7b3ab00c89\",\n  \"documentId\": \"INVOICE-2026-200\",\n  \"peppolDocumentType\": \"INVOICE\",\n  \"sender\": \"0208:1999999943\",\n  \"receiver\": \"0208:0552912569\",\n  \"details\": [],\n  \"notificationType\": \"INVOICE_RECEIVING\"\n}\n```\n\nThe notification ID and business identifiers are unchanged. V2 adds `notificationType`, makes the timestamp's\nUTC timezone explicit, uses `notificationDate` instead of the redundant `receivedDate`, and renames\n`sbdhTransmissionId` to `sbdhInstanceIdentifier`.\nThe [notification examples](#tag/Notification/operation/getNotificationsV2) illustrate 24 V2 models; deletion completion uses the additional shapes described below.\n\nFor V2 polling responses and webhook requests, verify that every notification has a recognized\n`notificationType`, the expected concrete model and a non-null `notificationId`. In particular, reject an empty\nunion wrapper or undecoded base object. Kiota consumers must perform these checks explicitly.\nDo not treat an unknown V2 type as V1. Retain an unsupported response for investigation, alert the integration\nowner and update the client/handlers before retrying; do not silently discard or acknowledge its items.\nResolve unsupported events before the [notification retention period](#section/Application-integration/Notifications-overview)\nexpires. For selected-event integrations, review\n[Handling new notification types and values](#section/Application-integration/Generating-your-API-client/Handling-new-notification-types-and-values).\n\n### Adopt registration outcomes\n\nV1 registration creation keeps its ID-only response. V2 creation, registration reads and registrations nested\nin V2 legal-entity responses expose `registrationStatus`, `registrationStatusMessage` and `activationDate`\nwhere applicable. Absent or inapplicable values can be omitted. A pending registration need not have an\nactivation date, and a successful POST does not by itself confirm activation.\n\nThese application-response excerpts show the migration-relevant lifecycle fields of one active registration\nwith fictional example data. They are taken from an item in the registration GET response's\n`peppolRegistrations` array. Other fields, including `creationDate` and `peppolRegistrationDetails`, and the\nresponse envelope are omitted for clarity.\n\n**V1 registration item — excerpt**\n\n```json\n{\n  \"peppolRegistrationId\": 1\n}\n```\n\n**V2 registration item — excerpt**\n\n```json\n{\n  \"peppolRegistrationId\": 1,\n  \"registrationStatus\": \"ACTIVE\",\n  \"activationDate\": \"2026-10-25T03:00:00.987Z\"\n}\n```\n\nThe same registration ID is retained; V2 exposes the lifecycle state and its UTC activation timestamp. `registrationStatusMessage` is absent in this successful example; handle it when present,\nfor example when `registrationStatus` is `FAILED`.\n\nFor French receiving registrations, observe completion through V2 registration reads or notifications.\nThese activation and failure notifications apply to France only, not to sender-only registrations.\nThe notification model is\n`LEGAL_ENTITY_PEPPOL_REGISTRATION`; `eventType` distinguishes `LEGAL_ENTITY_PEPPOL_REGISTRATION_ACTIVATED`\nfrom `LEGAL_ENTITY_PEPPOL_REGISTRATION_ACTIVATION_ERROR`. These outcomes are available through V2 polling\nand explicitly selected V2 webhooks, and are excluded from V1 notifications. See\n[registration creation](#tag/Legal-Entity-Peppol-Registration/operation/createPeppolRegistrationForLegalEntityV2).\n\nFrench deletion completion uses two additional V2 shapes: `LEGAL_ENTITY_PEPPOL_REGISTRATION_DELETED`\nand `LEGAL_ENTITY_DELETED`. Each uses the same value for `notificationType` and `eventType`.\nThe registration payload retains `legalEntityId`, `peppolRegistrationId` and `participantIdentifier`;\nthe company payload retains `legalEntityId`. Both include the normal `notificationId` and UTC\n`notificationDate`. That date records completed cleanup, not the earlier Annuaire closure date.\nNeither shape adds a registration activation status. Update generated V2 clients and receiver\ndispatch before processing these events. They are excluded from V1 polling and V1 webhooks.\n\n### Switch webhook delivery independently\n\nEnabled V2 settings updates selecting `payloadVersion: V2` require the receiver to acknowledge\n`WEBHOOK_VERIFICATION` before saving, unless that update explicitly passes `skipVerification=true`.\nSee [Webhook settings verification](#section/Application-integration/Webhook-settings-verification)\nfor the test payload, bypass and failure behavior. V1 settings requests and V1 payload configurations\nretain their existing behavior.\n\nPrepare your receiver to accept both V1 and V2 before changing the webhook payload setting. For an existing\nconfigured receiver, send a version-only PATCH so the URL, active state, authentication and single/bulk mode\nare preserved:\n\n```shell\ncurl --request PATCH \\\n  --header 'accessToken: YOUR_API_ACCESS_TOKEN' \\\n  --header 'Authorization: Basic YOUR_USERNAME_AND_PASSWORD_BASE64' \\\n  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \\\n  --data '{\"payloadVersion\":\"V2\"}' \\\n  'https://test-peppol-api1.ademico-software.com/domibus/api/peppol/v2/settings/webhooks'\n```\n\nA successful update returns **HTTP 204 with no response body**. Read the saved selection separately:\n\n```shell\ncurl --request GET \\\n  --header 'accessToken: YOUR_API_ACCESS_TOKEN' \\\n  --header 'Authorization: Basic YOUR_USERNAME_AND_PASSWORD_BASE64' \\\n  --header 'Accept: application/json' \\\n  'https://test-peppol-api1.ademico-software.com/domibus/api/peppol/v2/settings/webhooks'\n```\n\nCheck that `payloadVersion` is `V2` and that your other settings are unchanged. Omitted or null versions in\nsubsequent PUT/PATCH requests preserve an existing selection; switching back requires explicit `V1`.\nIf you change `bulk`, also deploy support for the corresponding request envelope. A single request is a bare\nnotification; bulk uses `{ \"pagination\": ..., \"notifications\": [...] }`. V2 bulk requests do not mix V1 and V2 items.\n\nSettings changes normally take effect promptly. If propagation is delayed, earlier settings can remain in use\nfor up to one hour with the default configuration, and requests already started can finish later. A GET confirms\nthe saved selection, not completion of the delivery transition. Keep both decoders until support confirms the\nnew settings apply to all deliveries and earlier attempts have finished; a quiet interval alone is insufficient.\n\nDetect V2 by the presence of `notificationType`; V1 does not contain that field. Inspect each notification in a\nbatch. Deduplicate by notification ID across polling and webhook deliveries, including both payload versions: after an explicit version\nchange, the same event can be retried in a different format. Return HTTP 200 only after successfully processing\nthe request; for a bulk request that acknowledges every item. Rejected deliveries follow the existing retry\npolicy, with no automatic downgrade. Exhausting webhook retries leaves the notification unacknowledged and\navailable to polling until it is acknowledged or deleted by [retention](#section/Application-integration/Notifications-overview).\nPolling acknowledgement and webhook success refer to the same event.\nSee [Selecting V2 webhook delivery](#section/Application-integration/Selecting-V2-webhook-delivery) for receiver details.\n\n### Verify the migration and retain a rollback path\n\nBefore using the updated integration in PROD, verify in TEST that:\n\n- Every REST call uses the documented V2 method and path, with any required request-model changes applied.\n- The generated client decodes your real responses and all notification types your business uses, including\n  failure outcomes, optional fields and nullable values. Test additional JSON properties separately from\n  unknown enum values/types, malformed IDs and undecoded notification wrappers.\n- UTC timestamps preserve the same instant when your application runs in different timezones. Date-only\n  invoice dates do not shift, and writable timestamps carry an offset.\n- Polling, single or bulk delivery, retries and acknowledgement update your business state once. Test a\n  version change with a pending/retried event and retain the same deduplication record across decoders.\n- French receiving registration creation is not mistaken for activation, and registration failure outcomes are handled.\n- Structured CDAR handling accepts HTTP 204 without attempting to decode a success body and handles both\n  documented HTTP 400 bodies. See [CDAR submission responses](#section/Application-integration/CDAR-submission-responses).\n- The V1 client/decoder is still available if you need to roll back, and notifications remain observable during\n  the entire transition.\n\nDuring the six-month V1 support window, you can roll back affected REST calls using the retained V1 client\nwith the original V1 methods and date formats. To roll back\nwebhooks, PATCH `{\"payloadVersion\":\"V1\"}` through the same settings endpoint and keep both decoders during\nthe reverse transition too. Do not use omission or null as a rollback request.\n\nSwitching versions does not recreate or replay acknowledged notifications. Pending French receiving registration outcome events\nare V2-only: keep a V2 polling consumer available if you still need those outcomes after returning webhooks to V1.\nPreserve notification IDs and processing records so rollback does not repeat business effects.\n\n## Dates and time zones\n\nAPI response timestamps use ISO 8601 in **UTC**, for example `2026-07-28T04:33:35.123Z`.\nThe `Z` suffix means UTC.\n\nWhen supplying a timestamp, include `Z` or an explicit offset such as `+02:00`.\nDo not send a local time without an offset.\n\n**Calendar dates** use `yyyy-MM-dd`, for example `2026-07-28`. They have no time or timezone\nand must not be shifted when converting between timezones.\n\nFollow each field's schema for additional requirements. Dates inside exchanged documents\nfollow the format defined by that document.\n\n## Generating your API client\n\nDownload the OpenAPI JSON associated with this documentation and save it as `openapi.json`.\nGenerate your client from the complete document and use the documented method and path for each operation.\n\nUse these language-specific settings for OpenAPI Generator **7.26.0**:\n\n```shell\njava -jar openapi-generator-cli-7.26.0.jar generate \\\n  -i openapi.json -g java --library okhttp-gson -o client-java \\\n  --additional-properties=disallowAdditionalPropertiesIfNotPresent=false \\\n  --additional-properties=dateLibrary=java8 \\\n  --additional-properties=legacyDiscriminatorBehavior=false \\\n  --additional-properties=useOneOfDiscriminatorLookup=true \\\n  --additional-properties=hideGenerationTimestamp=true\n\njava -jar openapi-generator-cli-7.26.0.jar generate \\\n  -i openapi.json -g csharp --library generichost -o client-csharp \\\n  --additional-properties=disallowAdditionalPropertiesIfNotPresent=false \\\n  --additional-properties=targetFramework=net8.0 \\\n  --additional-properties=useOneOfDiscriminatorLookup=true \\\n  --additional-properties=validatable=false \\\n  --additional-properties=hideGenerationTimestamp=true\n```\n\nThe C# `validatable=false` setting avoids the generator's model-validation compilation issue.\nIt disables generated model validation; it does not prove that a decoded object satisfies every schema\nconstraint. Validate required notification fields and supported types before processing or acknowledgement,\nand validate business inputs before submission. The server still validates submitted requests.\n\nUse the generated request models for CDAR dates and company timestamps. Configure Basic authentication or OAuth2 as described in\n[Authentication](#section/Authentication), and supply the required `accessToken` header on every request.\n\n### Accepting additional response fields\n\nConfigure clients to accept JSON properties they do not recognize. The API can add optional response fields\nwithin the same version. An existing client should continue reading the fields it knows when a later response\nalso contains a new property; this applies to nested objects and webhook payloads as well as top-level responses.\n\nThe commands above explicitly set `disallowAdditionalPropertiesIfNotPresent=false`. With OpenAPI Generator\n7.26.0, this lets the Java `okhttp-gson` and C# `generichost` clients accept extra properties when the schema\nallows them. The Java generator otherwise defaults to rejecting properties absent from its generated model,\neven when the OpenAPI schema has not forbidden them. The similarly named `failOnUnknownProperties=false`\noption applies to Jackson; it does not fix the Gson validation used in the Java command above. See the\n[Java generator options](https://openapi-generator.tech/docs/generators/java/) and\n[C# generator options](https://openapi-generator.tech/docs/generators/csharp/).\n\nRegenerate and deploy the client with these settings; changing a command or downloading a newer specification\ndoes not alter an already deployed SDK. Keep the generated serializers and validation of known fields.\nFor example, an extra property must not cause an error, but an object in place of an integer `notificationId`\nmust still be rejected. Before upgrading your generator, check that a representative response with extra\nproperties still decodes and preserves its known values.\n\nKiota's default C# and Java models retain extra properties through `AdditionalData`; use its generated parsing\nand serialization infrastructure and keep additional-data support enabled. See\n[Kiota serialization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openapi/kiota/serialization).\n\nAccepting an extra property does not make an unknown enum value or notification type safe to process.\nKeep the complete-response checks and handling described below; do not suppress decoding errors or silently\nacknowledge an unsupported notification.\n\n### Decoding notifications\n\nKiota **1.36.1** C# and Java clients also decode notifications, with an additional consumer check:\nvalidate the entire returned notification list before processing or acknowledging any item. Every business notification must\ncontain a recognized `notificationType`, decode into its corresponding concrete model and have a non-null\n`notificationId`. Kiota can decode a malformed integer ID as null, so explicitly reject a missing or null ID\nafter decoding. This check covers the notification identity; it is not full validation of every schema field.\nReject an empty union wrapper or an undecoded base object; retain the response for investigation and do not acknowledge its items.\nUnknown future notification types must be detected instead of silently discarded. Webhook receivers also handle\n`WEBHOOK_VERIFICATION` separately, using its `verificationId` and returning HTTP 2xx without business processing\nor a separate acknowledgement. This test has no `notificationId` and never appears in polling.\n\nJava and Kiota notification writers can omit required null properties when serializing received notifications\nagain. Use these clients to consume notifications; do not assume that reserialization preserves the original payload.\n\nNSwag **14.7.1** C# generation and compilation succeed, but automatic decoding of the polymorphic notification\nresponse is not supported by the verified configuration. A successful build alone does not establish notification\nsupport. Use OpenAPI Generator or Kiota with the consumer check above for this workflow.\n\n### Handling new notification types and values\n\nThe API can add fields, event values and notification types within the same version.\nA client that ignores extra JSON fields may still reject an unfamiliar enum value or notification type.\nWith the complete-response check above, an unsupported pending item can block repeated polling of the\nsame page. Repeating the request alone does not resolve it.\n\nIf a response cannot be decoded completely, retain it for investigation, alert the integration owner,\nand do not process or acknowledge its items.
