Update the generated client and the corresponding event\nhandlers, then retry polling and acknowledge only successfully handled events. Resolve this promptly\nbefore the [notification retention period](#section/Application-integration/Notifications-overview) expires;\npreserve the response so it can be investigated if it expires.\nUse notification IDs to avoid repeating business effects when retrying previously handled events.\n\nFor integrations that intentionally handle only selected events, use the documented `eventType` filter\nand expand it when the handlers are ready. Filtering can isolate new event values, but cannot isolate\nan unfamiliar notification type that shares an existing event value. Filtered-out events remain\nunprocessed and subject to retention. Do not discard or acknowledge them merely to unblock polling.\nReview API release notes and validate the client when adopting new fields, event values or types.\n\n## CDAR submission responses\n\nThe [structured CDAR operation](#tag/France-CDAR/operation/sendCDARV2) can return:\n\n| Status | Response |\n| --- | --- |\n| `200` | Submission details in `DocumentSubmissionResultRO`. |\n| `204` | Acceptance without a response body; do not attempt to deserialize a success model. |\n| `400` | `ApplicationMessage` with a message string for request parsing failures, or `FileSubmissionResultError` with a nested message object and an optional validation report for submission failures. |\n\nFor the flat error, read `code` and `message`. For the submission error, read `message.code`,\n`message.message` and, when present, `validationReport`. Acceptance is not confirmation of delivery;\ntrack subsequent results through notifications.\n\n## Notifications overview\n\nNotifications report document delivery, receipt, invoice lifecycle changes, reporting outcomes and company\nactivation results. `notificationType` identifies the JSON model; `eventType` identifies the event within that model.\nFor example, `INVOICE_SENDING` can report either `DOCUMENT_SENT` or `DOCUMENT_SEND_FAILED`.\n\nEvery notification uses `notificationDate` as its common event timestamp. Dates with a different meaning\ninclude `acknowledgementDate`, `activationDate` and CDAR `receiptDateTime`.\n\n**Retention and recovery:** the default notification retention period is **60 days from creation**, including\nunacknowledged notifications. Confirm the period applicable to your service with support. Exhausting webhook\nretries does not acknowledge a notification: it remains available through polling until it is acknowledged\nor deleted by retention. Repair the receiver or update the client/handlers, retrieve the pending notifications,\nand acknowledge only those successfully processed before that period expires.\n\nThe [notifications endpoint](#tag/Notification/operation/getNotificationsV2) provides a combined list example\nillustrating 24 concrete types, plus individual examples. The examples are application-produced responses from\nlocal scenarios with fictional business data. They show the actual fields, omitted values and pagination returned\nby the service. Individual scenarios are independent unless their identifiers explicitly link them.\n\nA delivery acknowledgement, a buyer's approval and a tax authority's acceptance are different outcomes.\nFor France reporting, distinguish acceptance for reporting, submission, technical acknowledgement and final\nprocessing. Interpret `success` together with `eventType`; an earlier successful stage does not promise a later one.\n\nAutomatic French `202` and `203` CDAR delivery notifications may arrive in either order, independently of\ninvoice availability. For both `CDAR_SENT` and `CDAR_SEND_FAILED`, `documentStatus` identifies the attempted\n`FR_RECEIVED` or `FR_MADE_AVAILABLE` milestone, which can differ from the invoice's current status.\nThe event type and error details identify delivery failures. If the referenced invoice is not yet available,\nits document and transmission identifiers are retained, while `referencedDocument.peppolDocumentType` may be `null`.\nThese automatic receipts are independent of optional positive Message Level Responses; rejected documents\ndo not produce a positive receipt CDAR. The availability milestone applies to both polling and webhooks\nwithout waiting for notification consumption or customer action; delayed `202` delivery does not block `203`.\n\nFrench receiving Peppol registration outcomes use `LEGAL_ENTITY_PEPPOL_REGISTRATION_ACTIVATED` or\n`LEGAL_ENTITY_PEPPOL_REGISTRATION_ACTIVATION_ERROR`, with `notificationType` set to\n`LEGAL_ENTITY_PEPPOL_REGISTRATION`. These France-only events apply to receiving registrations, not sender-only\nregistrations. Observe registration completion or failure through polling or webhooks configured with\n`payloadVersion: V2`.\n\n**France only — deletion notifications:** Annuaire-managed `0225` receiving registration deletions and\ntheir explicitly requested legal-entity deletions produce the following completion events. See\n[Delete a Peppol registration](#tag/Legal-Entity-Peppol-Registration/operation/deletePeppolRegistrationForLegalEntity)\nand [Delete a legal entity](#tag/Legal-Entity/operation/deleteLegalEntity) for acceptance, progress and\ncompletion conditions. These events are available through polling and webhooks explicitly configured\nwith `payloadVersion: V2`.\n\n| `notificationType` and `eventType` | Retained identity |\n| --- | --- |\n| `LEGAL_ENTITY_PEPPOL_REGISTRATION_DELETED` | `legalEntityId`, `peppolRegistrationId`, `participantIdentifier` |\n| `LEGAL_ENTITY_DELETED` | `legalEntityId` |\n\nBoth payloads include `notificationId` and UTC `notificationDate`. The date records completed cleanup,\nnot the earlier Annuaire closure date. The identifiers refer to the original deleted resource even when\nit is no longer readable. No success notification is emitted while its required removal remains unresolved.\nThese notifications do not apply to standalone `9957`, sender-only, unmanaged or non-French registration deletion.\n\nA whole-company request can produce managed-registration completion notifications while another child\nis still pending. Delivery order is not guaranteed. Retries keep the same stored `notificationId`; deduplicate\nit across polling and webhook deliveries. Acknowledge only events your application has successfully processed.\n\n## Pull Notifications (Polling)\n\nPoll [GET notifications](#tag/Notification/operation/getNotificationsV2) approximately once per minute or less\nfrequently, as appropriate for your integration. Use the documented filters and pagination to retrieve pending events.\n\n```shell\ncurl -X GET \\\n  -H \"accessToken: YOUR_API_ACCESS_TOKEN\" -H \"Authorization: Basic YOUR_USERNAME_AND_PASSWORD_BASE64\" \\\n  -H \"Accept: application/json\" \\\n  \"https://test-peppol-api1.ademico-software.com/domibus/api/peppol/v2/notifications?pageSize=100\"\n```\n\nFor example, an invoice-response event reports a buyer's approval of an invoice. The response includes the complete\nnotification and its pagination metadata:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"pagination\" : {\n    \"count\" : 1,\n    \"page\" : 0,\n    \"pageSize\" : 100\n  },\n  \"notifications\" : [ {\n    \"eventType\" : \"INVOICE_RESPONSE_RECEIVED\",\n    \"notificationId\" : 15,\n    \"transmissionId\" : \"b5acd8a4-2492-3d05-8c13-1d2ab3971628\",\n    \"notificationDate\" : \"2026-10-25T20:54:07.456Z\",\n    \"documentId\" : \"INVOICE-2026-100\",\n    \"peppolDocumentType\" : \"INVOICE\",\n    \"documentStatus\" : \"ACCEPTED\",\n    \"sender\" : \"0208:0552912569\",\n    \"receiver\" : \"0208:1999999943\",\n    \"invoiceResponse\" : {\n      \"invoiceResponseId\" : \"RESPONSE-2026-100\",\n      \"invoiceTransmissionId\" : \"b5acd8a4-2492-3d05-8c13-1d2ab3971628\",\n      \"responseCode\" : \"AP\",\n      \"effectiveDate\" : \"2026-07-02\",\n      \"invoiceClarifications\" : [ ]\n    },\n    \"details\" : [ ],\n    \"sbdhInstanceIdentifier\" : \"5354c3f0-07ff-376f-af27-e21ab2da04b8\",\n    \"notificationType\" : \"INVOICE_RESPONSE_RECEIVING\"\n  } ]\n}\n```\n\nValidate every notification before processing the response. After successfully updating your application,\nacknowledge each processed event using its `notificationId`:\n\n```shell\ncurl -X DELETE \\\n  -H \"accessToken: YOUR_API_ACCESS_TOKEN\" -H \"Authorization: Basic YOUR_USERNAME_AND_PASSWORD_BASE64\" \\\n  \"https://test-peppol-api1.ademico-software.com/domibus/api/peppol/v2/notifications/{notificationId}\"\n```\n\nPolling and webhooks share the same `notificationId` and acknowledgement state. Acknowledging a processed\nevent removes it from pending results; successful webhook delivery consumes the same event. Reading notifications\ndoes not consume them or change webhook settings. Do not acknowledge an event that could not be decoded or processed.\n\n\n## Selecting V2 webhook delivery\n\n1. **Prepare your receiver.** Choose the payload shape and generate its models:\n\n   - **Single notification** (`bulk: false`): use the [single-webhook OpenAPI](https://ademico-software.com/peppol-webhook-rest-api/openapi.json). The body is the notification itself.\n   - **Batch** (`bulk: true`): use the [bulk-webhook OpenAPI](https://ademico-software.com/peppol-webhook-rest-api/bulk/openapi.json). The body contains `pagination` and a `notifications` array.\n\n   Both include a webhook-only `WEBHOOK_VERIFICATION` test and the same business notification models as polling, including French receiving registration outcomes and deletion completion. See the [notification examples](#tag/Notification/operation/getNotificationsV2) and deletion completion section for their payload fields.\n\n2. **Prepare the receiver settings.** Choose the receiver URL (`webhookUrl`), authentication, delivery mode (`bulk`) and any additional headers. A replacement receiver must support the selected payload format.\n\n3. **Apply the configuration.** Use [PATCH webhook settings](#tag/Webhook-Settings-API/operation/patchNotificationSettings) (`PATCH /api/peppol/v2/settings/webhooks`) and include `payloadVersion: \"V2\"` together with any changed receiver settings in the same request. Include `active: true` when the receiver is ready. Send the required `accessToken` header with Basic authentication or OAuth2. The management URL alone does not select the payload version.\n\nFor an already-configured compatible receiver, a version-only PATCH preserves its current URL, active status, delivery mode, headers and authentication:\n\n```json\n{\"payloadVersion\": \"V2\"}\n```\n\nOmitting `payloadVersion` or sending null preserves the selected version in both PUT and PATCH. Unknown values are rejected without updating settings.\n\n## Webhook settings verification\n\n[Replace webhook settings](#tag/Webhook-Settings-API/operation/updateNotificationSettings) and\n[PATCH webhook settings](#tag/Webhook-Settings-API/operation/patchNotificationSettings) send a test before saving by default\nwhen the resulting settings have `active: true` and\n`payloadVersion: V2`. This also applies to partial updates that retain those existing values.\nPrepare your receiver to accept the test before making an eligible update; existing saved settings continue\nworking until changed. To save without testing on a particular update, pass the query parameter\n`skipVerification=true`. This skips both the receiver test and any OAuth2 token request, while required-field,\nURL/address, header and OAuth policy validation still apply. The parameter defaults to `false`, is not saved\nin the configuration and uses the same settings-update permissions. You accept saving an unverified receiver;\nthe next update requires verification again unless explicitly skipped.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"notificationType\": \"WEBHOOK_VERIFICATION\",\n  \"verificationId\": \"d2fe3a28-f66f-4e52-8c94-d06e1dd07cad\",\n  \"notificationDate\": \"2026-11-04T12:00:00.000Z\"\n}\n```\n\nThe test uses the proposed URL, headers and authentication. Bulk mode wraps this one item in the usual\n`notifications` array with `pagination: {\"page\": 0, \"pageSize\": 1, \"count\": 1}`. Treat it as a connectivity test:\nreturn HTTP 2xx without creating a business record or calling a notification acknowledgement endpoint.\nIt has no `notificationId` or `eventType` and is never returned by polling.\n\nThere is one attempt, with no automatic retry or redirect following. When OAuth2 is configured, its token\nrequest is also made once using the proposed credentials. Connection/read timeouts apply separately to each\nrequest. A rejection, timeout or authentication failure returns HTTP 400 with a validation error and preserves\nthe previous settings. A timeout can happen after your receiver accepted the test; a later settings request\ncreates a new test. Updating to `active: false` does not send one.\n\nThe error's `message` identifies whether verification failed during authentication or the receiver request.\nRecognized network failures include `timeout`, `DNS resolution failure`, `connection failure` or `TLS failure`;\nHTTP rejections include the remote status. Raw exception text, credentials and remote response bodies are\nomitted. Unrecognized failures retain a general message for the failing stage. For example:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"code\": \"GENERIC_VALIDATION_ERROR\",\n  \"message\": \"Webhook verification failed during receiver request (timeout). Previous settings were not changed.\"\n}\n```\n\n**When handling business notifications:**\n\n- Validate `notificationType` before processing and deduplicate by `notificationId` across polling and webhook deliveries. Acknowledge only successfully processed events; do not silently acknowledge an unsupported event.\n- Polling and webhooks share notification IDs and acknowledgement state. Settings changes do not create a second event or replay consumed notifications.\n- Rejected delivery follows the retry policy without automatically changing the selected payload format.\n\n**Settings changes:** changes normally take effect promptly. If propagation is delayed, deliveries and retries may use earlier settings for up to one hour with the default configuration. Already-started requests may finish using earlier settings even after that interval. GET settings returns the explicitly selected `payloadVersion`; it confirms the saved selection, not that every delivery already uses it.\n\n## Push Notifications (Webhooks)\n\nWhen you choose to be notified via push notifications (webhooks), we deliver the notification directly to your\napplication. Implement a receiver using the\n[single-webhook reference](https://ademico-software.com/peppol-webhook-rest-api/) or\n[bulk-webhook reference](https://ademico-software.com/peppol-webhook-rest-api/bulk/), and configure it as described in\n[Selecting V2 webhook delivery](#section/Application-integration/Selecting-V2-webhook-delivery).\n\nFor example, when a buyer accepts your invoice, the receiver gets the invoice-response notification shown in\n[Pull Notifications (Polling)](#section/Application-integration/Pull-Notifications-(Polling)). A single webhook\nbody contains the notification itself; a bulk webhook contains `pagination` and a `notifications` array.\n\nWe expect that you return status `200` which indicates us that you have successfully processed the webhook.\nIf you return a different status, we retry delivery every 30 minutes for a maximum of 6 hours.\n\n> **NOTE** Please make sure to you allow traffic from our servers in your firewall rules. We will provide you the static\n> IP we use\n> to call your service webhooks.\n\nYou can refer to the [Notifications Endpoint](#tag/Notification/operation/getNotificationsV2) documentation to see the\ntypes of notifications we can push to you.\n\n\n# Country Specifics\n\n## France self-billing\n\nThe [UBL](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/submitUblFile),\n[CII](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/submitCiiFile) and\n[Factur-X](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/submitFacturXFile) submission endpoints support France self-billing\ndocuments in UBL 2.1, native CII D22B, and Factur-X EN16931 formats. No additional request parameter is required: the\nAPI detects self-billing from the invoice type code (BT-3) in the submitted document.\n\n| Document format | BT-3 XML element | Self-billing codes |\n|---|---|---|\n| UBL Invoice | `cbc:InvoiceTypeCode` | `389`, `500`, `501`, `471`, `473` |\n| UBL Credit Note | `cbc:CreditNoteTypeCode` | `261`, `502` |\n| CII D22B and Factur-X EN16931 | `rsm:CrossIndustryInvoice/rsm:ExchangedDocument/ram:TypeCode` | `389`, `500`, `501`, `471`, `473`, `261`, `502` |\n\nThe supported BT-3 values have the following meanings:\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `389` | Self-billed invoice |\n| `500` | Self-billed prepayment invoice |\n| `501` | Factored self-billed invoice |\n| `471` | Corrective self-billed invoice |\n| `473` | Factored corrective self-billed invoice |\n| `261` | Self-billed credit note |\n| `502` | Factored self-billed credit note |\n\nFor a detected self-billing document, the Buyer is the sender and the Seller is the receiver. Therefore, when submitting\nsuch a document, your registered local legal entity must be the Buyer and the Seller is the Peppol recipient. The Seller\nremains the issuer of the invoice or credit note. The API uses the following parties for routing:\n\n| Document format | Sender (Buyer) | Receiver (Seller) |\n|---|---|---|\n| UBL | `cac:AccountingCustomerParty` | `cac:AccountingSupplierParty` |\n| CII and Factur-X | `ram:BuyerTradeParty` | `ram:SellerTradeParty` |\n\nFrance self-billing documents continue to use the normal France customization and regulated or non-regulated profile\nidentifiers listed in [Supported Peppol documents](#section/Supported-Peppol-documents). Do not replace them with the\nPeppol BIS Self-Billing identifiers. Related document notifications expose `selfBilling: true`, and the France CDAR and\nPPF/C5 processing automatically follows the detected self-billing direction.\n\nIf BT-3 is missing, blank, or not one of the applicable codes above, the document keeps the normal Seller-to-Buyer\ndirection. For UBL, the Invoice and Credit Note code sets are separate; for example, code `261` does not identify a UBL\nInvoice as self-billing.\n\n## Getting started with Peppol in France\n\nFrance is rolling out mandatory B2B e-invoicing starting September 2026.  \n\nThe authoritative source for France's e-invoicing documentation is available at: [https://www.impots.gouv.fr/specifications-externes-b2b](https://www.impots.gouv.fr/specifications-externes-b2b)\n\nWhen working with France-specific flows, keep in mind the following differences from other countries:\n\n#### Legal entities\n\nWhen registering a legal entity for France-specific Peppol flows, you must provide both the platform/participant identifiers used for Peppol routing and the legal identifiers required for regulatory reporting.\n\n**Participant identifier schemes**\n\nFrance uses specific identifier schemes:\n-   The **Peppol participant identifier** typically uses the scheme `0225`, eg `0225:123456789` where `123456789` is the SIREN number of the company. This identifier is used as electronic address in the context of the French Continuous Transactional Control reform on e-invoicing. Variations using the SIRET number, a suffix or an additional routing code are possible. \n-   A **legal identifier** with scheme `0002` (SIREN) is required when registering the legal entity to enable France-specific regulatory reporting (e.g., e-reporting submissions to PPF).\n \n**Partial example JSON payload (create FR legal entity)**\n\n```json\n{\n  \"legalEntityDetails\": {\n    \"name\": \"ADEMICO SOFTWARE SRL\",\n    \"countryCode\": \"FR\",\n    \"legalIdentifiers\": [\n      {\n        \"scheme\": \"0002\",\n        \"identifier\": \"123456789\"\n      }\n    ],\n    \"publishInPeppolDirectory\": true,\n    \"registrationDate\": \"2026-01-19T14:56:22.000Z\",\n    \"websiteURL\": \"https://ademico-software.com\"\n  },\n  \"peppolRegistrations\": [\n    {\n      \"peppolIdentifier\": {\n        \"scheme\": \"0225\",\n        \"identifier\": \"123456789\"\n      },\n      \"peppolRegistration\": true,\n      \"supportedDocuments\": [...]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n> **Notes on the example**\n> - The `0225` participant identifier and the `0002` legal identifier both use the company SIREN (9 digits) in this example.\n> - For invoice-receiving registrations using scheme `0225`, `supportedDocuments` must include all the document types required in France, even if you do not expect to use all of them. For `0225` sender-only registrations, use the capability profile described below.\n> - Other permitted participant schemes, such as `9957` (French VAT), do not require the French document types. They still require a non-empty `supportedDocuments` list and must satisfy the country/scheme validation.\n\n---\n\n#### Register a France 0225 identifier for sending only\n\nA French legal entity that sends invoices but does not receive invoices can register a dedicated sender-only participant\nidentifier. The participant remains registered in SML/SMP so that it can receive French invoice lifecycle responses,\nbut it does not need a receiving line in the France Annuaire.\n\nUse the following values for a sender-only registration:\n\n* Set the legal entity `countryCode` to `FR`.\n* Use participant scheme `0225`.\n* Format the participant identifier as `<SIREN>_<suffix>`, where `<SIREN>` is exactly 9 digits and `<suffix>` is\n  non-empty free text. The general participant identifier restrictions also apply: spaces, dots and colons are not\n  allowed. For example: `123456789_SENDER`.\n* Set `peppolRegistration` to `true`. This flag means that our API manages the participant in SML/SMP; it does not mean\n  that the participant can receive invoices.\n* Include `FR_CDAR_REGULATED` in `supportedDocuments`; it is mandatory. You may additionally include\n  `FR_CDAR_NONREGULATED`, which is optional. Non-regulated CDAR alone does not qualify as sender-only.\n* You may also include `PEPPOL_MESSAGE_LEVEL_RESPONSE_TRANSACTION_3_0` and/or\n  `PEPPOL_INVOICE_RESPONSE_TRANSACTION_3_0`. These optional capabilities are not added automatically.\n* Do not include invoice, credit note or other receiving capabilities. If any such capability is present, the\n  registration is treated as a normal France receiving participant and the normal France capability and Annuaire rules\n  apply.\n\n`publishInPeppolDirectory` controls publication in the Peppol Directory independently; it does not create a receiving\nline in the France Annuaire.\n\nYou can create the legal entity and its sender-only registration together using\n[Create a legal entity](#tag/Legal-Entity/operation/createLegalEntityV2):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"legalEntityDetails\": {\n    \"name\": \"EXAMPLE COMPANY\",\n    \"countryCode\": \"FR\",\n    \"legalIdentifiers\": [\n      {\n        \"scheme\": \"0002\",\n        \"identifier\": \"123456789\"\n      }\n    ],\n    \"publishInPeppolDirectory\": false\n  },\n  \"peppolRegistrations\": [\n    {\n      \"peppolIdentifier\": {\n        \"scheme\": \"0225\",\n        \"identifier\": \"123456789_SENDER\"\n      },\n      \"peppolRegistration\": true,\n      \"supportedDocuments\": [\n        \"FR_CDAR_REGULATED\"\n      ]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nIf the French legal entity already exists, use\n[Register a legal entity in the Peppol network](#tag/Legal-Entity-Peppol-Registration/operation/createPeppolRegistrationForLegalEntityV2)\nwith the following request body:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"peppolRegistrationDetails\": {\n    \"peppolIdentifier\": {\n      \"scheme\": \"0225\",\n      \"identifier\": \"123456789_SENDER\"\n    },\n    \"peppolRegistration\": true,\n    \"supportedDocuments\": [\n      \"FR_CDAR_REGULATED\"\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\nThe same capability rules apply when updating the registration. Requests without mandatory `FR_CDAR_REGULATED` are\nrejected before SMP publication; it is not added automatically. A sender-only registration is published in SMP with\nregulated CDAR and any supplied non-regulated CDAR or optional public response capabilities. It is not registered as an invoice receiver in the France Annuaire.\n\nIf your French `0225` registration contains only optional response capabilities and omits regulated CDAR, creation or\nupdate returns `LEGAL_ENTITY_ERROR` explaining that `FR_CDAR_REGULATED` must be included in `supportedDocuments`.\nAdd regulated CDAR to correct a sender-only request; you do not need to add invoice-receiving capabilities.\n\nFor regulated French invoices between `0225` identifiers, this sender-only exception applies both when submitting an\ninvoice through the API and when receiving an invoice from Peppol. For API submissions, we check the stored registration\nmatching the sender's scheme and identifier: it must have the sender-only capability profile described above, regardless\nof whether `peppolRegistration` is `true` or `false`. That flag controls SMP management, not outgoing sender-only\nclassification. No sender SMP lookup is needed for this check. For incoming invoices, we check the external sender's\ncomplete SMP capability set instead. When the applicable check confirms the sender-only profile, the sender's Annuaire\nreceiving line is not required. When submitting, the sender's Annuaire platform\ncomparison is also skipped, but the sender must still be registered and available through your API credentials and pass the normal submission\nchecks. The receiver must still have a valid Annuaire entry. If the sender advertises other document capabilities or its\nsender-only profile cannot be confirmed from the applicable source, the normal Annuaire checks remain in place.\n\nCDAR lifecycle responses can be sent back to a sender-only invoice issuer without an Annuaire receiving line. CDAR\nsubmissions do not perform the invoice-specific Annuaire checks on either party. The sending participant must still be\nregistered and available through your API credentials, the document must pass the normal submission validations, and the receiver must advertise\nthe corresponding CDAR capability and process in SMP. This applies to API-submitted and automatically generated CDARs.\n\n---\n\n#### Supported documents\n\nThe list of supported documents for France is specific. When registering a legal entity, the following document types are typically supported:\n\nUBL Documents:\n*   `FR_UBL_INVOICE_CIUS_REGULATED`\n*   `FR_UBL_INVOICE_CIUS_NONREGULATED`\n*   `FR_UBL_INVOICE_EXTENSION_REGULATED`\n*   `FR_UBL_INVOICE_EXTENSION_NONREGULATED`\n*   `FR_UBL_CREDIT_NOTE_CIUS_REGULATED`\n*   `FR_UBL_CREDIT_NOTE_CIUS_NONREGULATED`\n*   `FR_UBL_CREDIT_NOTE_EXTENSION_REGULATED`\n*   `FR_UBL_CREDIT_NOTE_EXTENSION_NONREGULATED`\n\nCII (Cross Industry Invoice) Documents:\n*   `FR_CII_INVOICE_CIUS_REGULATED`\n*   `FR_CII_INVOICE_CIUS_NONREGULATED`\n*   `FR_CII_INVOICE_EXTENSION_REGULATED`\n*   `FR_CII_INVOICE_EXTENSION_NONREGULATED`\n*   `FR_FACTUR_X_REGULATED`\n*   `FR_FACTUR_X_NONREGULATED`\n\nAcknowledgement/Response Documents:\n*   `FR_CDAR_REGULATED`\n*   `FR_CDAR_NONREGULATED`\n\n> **Note:** For France CII and CDAR documents, we use the official schemas version `D22B` published by UNECE here: [https://unece.org/trade/documents/2023/06/standards/cross-industry-invoice-d22b](https://unece.org/trade/documents/2023/06/standards/cross-industry-invoice-d22b) and here: [https://unece.org/trade/documents/2023/07/standards/cross-domain-acknowledgement-and-response-d22b](https://unece.org/trade/documents/2023/07/standards/cross-domain-acknowledgement-and-response-d22b)\n>\n> For creating your CII invoice or credit note, use the **uncoupled CII D22B XSDs** from the [official UNECE package](https://unece.org/sites/default/files/2025-07/CII_D22B.zip), located in the ZIP file under: `XSD/uncoupled/Schema/uncefact`.\n> \n> For creating your CII invoice or credit note for Factur-X, use the **Factur-X XSDs** from [fnfe-mpe.org](https://fnfe-mpe.org/ressources/), located in the section `Les Schematrons des profils EN16931 et EXTENDED-CTC-FR ainsi que ceux des règles de gestion additionnelles France BR-FR-CTC, développés par le FNFE-MPE`.\n\n---\n\n#### PA responsibilities towards PPF\n\nIn the French model, the `PA` (*Plateforme agréée*) is the platform through which participants exchange invoices and related France-specific lifecycle messages, while the `PPF` is the French authority platform that receives regulatory reporting.\n\nFor B2B exchanges between French legal entities, it is the responsibility of the `PA` to report the exchanged documents to `PPF`. This means that you continue to send and receive your invoices through Peppol as usual, and we, acting as the platform, perform the corresponding reporting to `PPF` automatically without requiring any extra action from you. We also notify you (the seller) about these authority submissions through the France `PPF / C5` notifications described in the section below.\n\nThe following table details exactly what we report to `PPF` and when, for B2B exchanges:\n\n| What is reported to PPF | When                                                                                 | Initiation | Your role |\n|---|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---|---|\n| The invoice (or credit note) | When you send a Peppol invoice through our platform                                  | Triggered by your invoice submission | Seller |\n| Lifecycle status `Déposée` | At the same time as the invoice submission - confirms the invoice has been deposited | Automatic by our platform (`PA`) | Seller |\n| Lifecycle status `Rejetée` | At the same time as the invoice submission, if the invoice is rejected at submission | Automatic by our platform (`PA`) | Seller |\n| Lifecycle status `Refusée` | When you send a Peppol invoice response with status *Refused*                        | Initiated by you (user action) | Buyer |\n| Lifecycle status `Encaissée` | When you send a Peppol invoice response with status *Collected*                      | Initiated by you (user action) | Seller |\n\n> **Note:** Other lifecycle statuses, such as `Approuvée`, `Mise à disposition`, `Prise en charge`, or `Paiement transmis`, may be supported and exchanged between platforms where applicable. However, under the French e-invoicing reform, the statuses that must be reported to the `PPF` for regulatory purposes are `Déposée`, `Rejetée`, `Refusée`, and, where payment reporting is required, `Encaissée`. The `Encaissée` status is mandatory only for transactions where payment data must be reported, for example where VAT is due on cash receipt.\n\nFor an accepted regulated French invoice or credit note, our platform automatically sends a\n`202` (`Reçue par la plateforme`) CDAR to the original sender after reception controls succeed.\nThis applies to supported UBL, CII and Factur-X documents, including self-billing. It confirms\nacceptance by the receiving platform; it does not confirm that the customer has read or approved\nthe invoice. A rejected document does not produce this positive receipt response. The `202`\nresponse is independent of optional positive Message Level Responses and is not reported to PPF.\n\nFor the same accepted documents, our platform automatically sends a `203` (`Mise à disposition`)\nCDAR once the invoice content and its `DOCUMENT_RECEIVED` notification are available to you\nthrough the API in your workspace. The response records that availability time. This milestone\nis the same for PUSH and PULL notifications: it does not wait for successful webhook delivery,\nyour first poll, notification consumption or invoice download. It does not indicate that you\nhave read or approved the invoice. A delayed `202` response does not delay making the invoice\navailable or sending its `203` response; a delayed `203` response does not prevent you from\naccessing the invoice. Neither `202` nor `203` is reported to PPF.\n\nFor B2C transactions, and also for B2B transactions where the buyer is not a legal company residing in France, the reporting is not triggered automatically from the Peppol exchange flow. In these cases, it is your responsibility to use the dedicated [France e-reporting endpoint](#tag/France-PPF-Submission/operation/submitFranceEReportingXmlForLegalEntity) to submit the reporting payload to `PPF`.\n\n---\n\n#### Validation before sending an invoice or credit note\n\nFor submissions whose sender is registered in France under Peppol scheme `0225`,\nwith automatic PPF reporting enabled, validation runs in this order:\n\n1. Validate the original UBL or CII XML, or the XML embedded in a Factur-X PDF, against its source XSD and Schematron rules.\n2. Prepare an independent PPF Flux 1 Full extraction using the reporting mappings and identifier filtering.\n3. Validate the extraction against the PPF Full XSD and F1 Schematron, then dispatch the unchanged original document through Peppol.\n\nThis covers UBL invoices and credit notes, CII, and Factur-X EN16931 and Extended,\nincluding applicable self-billing, where the buyer is the sender. Other sender\nschemes, such as `9957` or `0088`, bypass this F1 check even with explicit\n`X-C5-REPORTING: true`; source-document validation still applies.\nLocally detectable preparation or validation\nerrors return HTTP 400 before dispatch. The error identifies the document and,\nwhen available, the affected field or location and rule. Extraction validation\nfailures include a structured `validationReport` for the generated extraction,\nwith the corresponding `XML_VALIDATION_ERROR`, `XSD_VALIDATION_ERROR` or\n`SCHEMATRON_VALIDATION_ERROR` code. F1 Schematron messages include rule references\nin their descriptions and separate XPath locations; `errorId` may be empty. Correct the input before submitting it again.\n\nWhen `X-C5-REPORTING` is omitted, the existing France reporting policy applies:\nregulated invoices and credit notes use automatic reporting; non-regulated ones\ndo not. Explicit `true` requests automatic reporting. Explicit `false` disables\nautomatic reporting and the F1 extraction check; source validation still applies.\n\nPPF reporting takes place asynchronously after successful Peppol sending.\nPassing validation does not guarantee PPF acceptance. Follow the C5 notifications\nbelow for the final reporting outcome.\n\n---\n\n#### Notifications\n\nSimilar to other countries, you will receive notifications when sending and receiving documents.  \nAfter a document (e.g. an invoice) is sent, you will receive a `DOCUMENT_SENT` notification. You can then use the `transmissionId` from the notification to retrieve the transport evidence, which serves as proof of delivery to the recipient's platform.  \nWhen you receive a document (e.g. an invoice), you will get a `DOCUMENT_RECEIVED` notification. You can then use the `transmissionId` from the notification to retrieve the received document content in its original format (either UBL XML, CII XML or Factur-X PDF).\n\nFrance also introduces notification types that are specific to the French document lifecycle and French authority reporting flows.\n\n##### CDAR notifications\n\n`CDAR` stands for Cross Domain Acknowledgement And Response. In practice, these notifications are used for France-specific invoice lifecycle updates exchanged over Peppol.\n\n*   `CDAR_SENT`: a France lifecycle CDAR message was successfully sent by our platform. This is different from `DOCUMENT_SENT`, which confirms that the original invoice or credit note was delivered to the recipient Access Point. `CDAR_SENT` is about the lifecycle response itself. For example, when a France invoice is successfully sent, we as a platform (`PA`) will also send a seller-side `Déposée` CDAR in the France flow.\n*   `CDAR_RECEIVED`: a France lifecycle CDAR message was received by our platform for a previously sent or received document. This notification means that the referenced invoice or credit note has received a France-specific status update. For example, after the buyer receives an invoice, they might send a `Rejetée` CDAR back to the seller, which would trigger a `CDAR_RECEIVED` notification for the seller.\n\n##### PPF / C5 reporting notifications\n\nPPF reporting is asynchronous and independent of Peppol delivery. A `DOCUMENT_SENT` notification confirms delivery to the recipient's Access Point; it does not confirm reporting to PPF. PPF entries are sent in bulk, but you receive notifications for each individual invoice, credit note, CDAR or e-reporting payload.\n\nA typical successful lifecycle is `C5_DOCUMENT_ENQUEUED` &rarr; `C5_DOCUMENT_SUBMITTED` &rarr; `C5_DOCUMENT_ACKNOWLEDGED` &rarr; `C5_DOCUMENT_PROCESSED`:\n\n| Event type | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `C5_DOCUMENT_ENQUEUED` | The individual entry was created and is waiting to be included in a PPF bulk submission. It has not yet been sent to PPF. |\n| `C5_DOCUMENT_SUBMITTED` | The bulk archive containing the entry was uploaded to PPF. This confirms transport only, not technical or business acceptance. |\n| `C5_DOCUMENT_SUBMISSION_FAILED` | The entry could not be prepared/queued, or its bulk archive could not be uploaded after all retries. `details` contains the available error information. A manual resubmission starts a new reporting lifecycle. |\n| `C5_DOCUMENT_ACKNOWLEDGED` | PPF returned technical status `500` (*Recevable*). The archive passed PPF's initial checks, but business processing is not yet complete. |\n| `C5_DOCUMENT_NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED` | PPF returned technical status `501` (*Irrecevable*). The archive failed PPF's initial checks; rejection information is returned when supplied by PPF. |\n| `C5_DOCUMENT_PROCESSED` | PPF completed business processing successfully (`250` for e-invoicing or `300` for e-reporting). |\n| `C5_DOCUMENT_PROCESSING_FAILED` | PPF completed processing with a business rejection (`251` for e-invoicing, `301` for e-reporting or `601` for a lifecycle report). |\n\nUse the notification fields as follows:\n\n*   `submissionId` identifies the individual PPF entry; `c5TransmissionId` identifies the outbound bulk archive and is therefore normally absent from the initial `C5_DOCUMENT_ENQUEUED` notification.\n*   On PPF response notifications, `acknowledgementId` is the name of the incoming PPF acknowledgement or business-response archive that produced the notification.\n*   For invoices, credit notes and CDAR responses sent through Peppol, use `transmissionId` to correlate the C5 notification with the corresponding Peppol document submission.\n*   Standalone France e-reporting submissions do not have a Peppol `transmissionId`. Correlate their notifications using the `submissionId` returned when the e-reporting submission was initially accepted.\n*   `success` describes the outcome of the current event, not the final outcome of the entire lifecycle. General errors are returned in `details`; PPF business or validation reasons can be returned in `documentStatus`, `documentStatusDetails` and their nested `notes`.\n\nFields that do not apply to the current stage may be omitted. PPF acknowledgements and business responses arrive later, so consumers should use `eventType` and the identifiers above rather than assuming that the notifications will be returned together.\n\n---\n\n##### Detailed France exchange walkthrough\n\nThe following example shows a typical France invoice exchange and the related CDAR and PPF/C5 notifications end to end.\n\nAlthough this flow is representative of real-world exchanges, it is intentionally detailed to illustrate a longer end-to-end scenario. It is not the minimal possible example. represent the unique identifier of a participant in\nthe Peppol network. For instance the participant scheme and identifier of Ademico Software is `0208:0522912569`.\n\nThe **participant scheme** describes the **participant identifier** type eg VAT number, Chamber of Commerce number, GLN\nnumber, etc. The participant scheme is usually specific to each country eg for Belgium is `0208` which is the enterprise\nnumber but you can also have an\ninternationally used scheme eg GLN number.\nThe complete list of Peppol participant schemes can be\nfound <a href=\"https://docs.peppol.eu/edelivery/codelists\" target=\"_blank\">on the Peppol website</a> under\nsection `Participant Identifier Schemes`.\n\nThe **participant identifier** can be the participant's VAT number, Chamber of Commerce number, GLN, etc. For instance\nthe\nparticipant number of Ademico Software is the enterprise number from the Belgian Crossroad Bank of Enterprises which is\n0552912569.\n\nA legal entity can be registered in the Peppol network multiple times using different identifiers. For instance a legal\nentity in Belgium can be registered with the company registration number 0208:0552912569 and with the Belgium VAT number\n9925:BE0552912569.\n\nHere are some examples of Peppol identifiers in different countries:\n\n<table>\n  <tr>\n    <th>Country</th>\n    <th>Peppol identifiers</th>\n  </tr>\n  <tr>\n        <td>Belgium</td>\n        <td>\n            <ul>\n <td>\n        <p>0225 is the scheme used in France for identifiers used as electronic addresses in the context of the French Continuous Transactional Control reform on e-invoicing.</p>\n        <p>The identifier value permits only ASCII letters, digits, hyphens and underscores. Dots and @ are rejected for both receiving and sender-only registrations before Annuaire creation or Peppol publication.</p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>0225:123456789 is the most common form you'll encounter in practice: 0225 followed by the SIREN number of the company</li>\n          <li>0225:123456789_12345678900001 is the form merging both the SIREN and SIRET number of the legal entity (allows companies to track invoices at the level of each establishment)</li>\n          <li>0225:123456789_A1234 is used to address a specific department, at the company level; it is formed by SIREN followed by a SUFFIX</li>\n          <li>0225:123456789_12345678900001_X123 is used to address a specific department of a specific establishment of the company; it is formed by SIREN followed by SIRET followed by a ROUTINGCODE</li>\n        </ul>\n        <p>Other identifiers used in the context of the French e-invoicing are:</p>\n        <ul>\n          <li>0002:123456789 - the SIREN of the company (9 digits)</li>\n          <li>0009:12345678900001 - the SIRET of the establishment (14 digits)</li>\n          <li>9957:FR123456789 - the VAT number of the company</li>\n        </ul>\n      </td>\n    </tr>\n\n</table>\n\n# Changelog\n\n- 2.0\n    - **API token header:** send `accessToken` in the HTTP header with every request and remove it from the URL query. Requests containing the query parameter are rejected. See the [migration guide](#section/Application-integration/Migrating-from-V1-to-V2).\n    - **Migration from V1 to V2:** V2 provides all public REST operations under `/api/peppol/v2`. Existing V1 integrations should follow the [migration guide](#section/Application-integration/Migrating-from-V1-to-V2). All public V1 REST operations and V1 webhook payloads will retire six months after the complete V2 API becomes available in production. New integrations can start directly with V2.\n    - **Authentication errors:** France PPF submissions and XML downloads now return HTTP 401 for missing, invalid or expired authentication credentials, so integrations can distinguish authentication failures from invalid report content.\n    - **Consistent SBDH identifiers:** document search, notifications and IRAS receipts use `sbdhInstanceIdentifier`. When migrating from V1, update the former `sbdhTransmissionId` fields and document-search parameter; identifier values and the documents they identify are unchanged.\n    - **Unambiguous dates:** response timestamps use UTC with a `Z` suffix. Send writable timestamps with `Z` or an explicit offset. Calendar dates, including CDAR `issueDate`, use `yyyy-MM-dd`.\n    - **Webhook settings verification:** before changing an enabled configuration with `payloadVersion: V2` through the current settings API, your receiver must accept a `WEBHOOK_VERIFICATION` test by default. Use `skipVerification=true` for an individual update when you accept saving an unverified receiver; local validation still applies. A failed test preserves the previous settings, with network failure categories explained in the error message. See [webhook verification](#section/Application-integration/Webhook-settings-verification).\n    - **Notification handling:** notifications include `notificationType` to identify their payload model and use the common `notificationDate`. Polling accepts multiple `eventType` filters. For webhooks, explicitly select `payloadVersion: V2`; changing REST URLs or polling does not select the webhook format.\n    - **Automatic French receipts:** accepted regulated French invoices and credit notes, including supported UBL, CII, Factur-X and self-billing documents, generate `202` (`Reçue par la plateforme`) after reception controls pass and `203` (`Mise à disposition`) when the document and its receipt notification become accessible through the API. Availability does not wait for webhook delivery, polling or download; neither status is reported to PPF. Delivery notifications can arrive in either order; see [notification handling](#section/Application-integration/Notifications-overview).\n    - **French Legal Entity receiving registrations:** Legal Entity registrations are not immediately available on Peppol. Annuaire activation is normally scheduled for the day after the request and may take longer; the participant is registered on Peppol only after that activation is confirmed. Track the status through registration details or receive these notifications through V2 polling and webhooks:\n        - `eventType: LEGAL_ENTITY_PEPPOL_REGISTRATION_ACTIVATED` confirms that the receiving registration is active.\n        - `eventType: LEGAL_ENTITY_PEPPOL_REGISTRATION_ACTIVATION_ERROR` reports a confirmed activation failure; check the notification details.\n    - **France Annuaire routing codes:** create, find, update and deactivate routing codes for your legal entity's SIRETs. Codes referenced by current or future directory entries cannot be deactivated.\n    - **France Annuaire search accuracy:** SIREN/SIRET searches omit registrations canceled by an Annuaire mask. France regulated-invoice validation also ignores masked participant lines, so a canceled address is not treated as active.\n    - **French deletion sequencing and progress:** Annuaire-managed `0225` receiving deletions now wait for confirmed Annuaire closure before Peppol removal. HTTP 200 can mean accepted and still pending; affected registrations remain visible while confirmation or Peppol removal is outstanding. V2 details expose `deletionStatus`: `PENDING` for outstanding confirmation or cleanup, or `ACTION_REQUIRED` when support is needed.\n    - **French deletion completion:** V2 notifications confirm when an Annuaire-managed `0225` receiving registration or its explicitly requested legal-entity deletion has finished. Receive individual registration outcomes and final company completion through V2 polling or explicitly selected V2 webhooks. See [Delete a Peppol registration](#tag/Legal-Entity-Peppol-Registration/operation/deletePeppolRegistrationForLegalEntity) and [Delete a legal entity](#tag/Legal-Entity/operation/deleteLegalEntity).\n    - **Readable PDF downloads:** download PDFs of retained sent and received invoices and credit notes. Existing PDFs are preferred, with optional generation, language and layout controls for supported profiles. See the [PDF download options](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/getInvoiceInPdfFormat).\n    - **UBL downloads:** download supported CII and Factur-X invoices and credit notes as UBL, for both sent and received documents. Existing UBL files are returned unchanged. Unsupported conversions are rejected; conversion does not replace invoice validation.\n    - **Factur-X support:** BASIC WL, EN16931 and Extended validation supports Factur-X 1.09.2.\n    - **Integration guidance:** guides are organized around getting started, common integration tasks and country-specific requirements, with complete notification examples to help build your receiver.\n\n- 1.23 - September 2026\n    - **Generated-client compatibility correction:** restored the historical OpenAPI date-time types and shared document-type enum reference. API payloads, date serialization, request parsing and nullable unresolved document types are unchanged. Response timestamps remain offset-less UTC values; see [Dates and time zones](#section/Application-integration/Dates-and-time-zones) for the exact formats and client parser configuration. Regenerating clients that adopted the string or property-specific enum types can require source changes.\n    - Received CDAR notifications preserve the referenced invoice or credit-note identifier even when invoice reception was rejected before a transmission was recorded. When no associated invoice or credit note is available, its document type and unresolved transmission identifier are null. The CDAR's business type code is not used to infer the original document format.\n    - Invoice and credit-note submissions whose sender is registered in France under Peppol scheme `0225`, with automatic PPF reporting enabled, now prepare and validate the independent Flux 1 extraction before Peppol dispatch. Locally detectable mapping, XSD and F1 Schematron errors reject the submission. Extraction validation failures include a structured `validationReport` with rule references and locations when available. UBL, CII, Factur-X EN16931 and Extended are covered, including applicable self-billing. The original document is preserved; PPF reporting and acceptance remain asynchronous.\n    - Fixed French invoice submissions with explicit `X-C5-REPORTING: true`. Explicit false continues to disable automatic reporting and the Flux 1 preparation check.\n    - France e-reporting submissions now validate F10 Schematron rules before acceptance. Invalid files return HTTP 400 with a structured validation report and failed rule details. Invoice identifiers, including references to previous invoices, are limited to 20 characters.\n    - Limited mandatory French supported-document validation to registrations using scheme `0225`. Other permitted schemes, including French VAT (`9957`), can register Peppol BIS Billing capabilities without the French document set. Existing `0225` sender-only requirements remain unchanged.\n- 1.22 - September 2026\n    - Corrected French PPF lifecycle reports for consolidated credit notes: referenced invoice type `262` is reported as `381`, consistently with the invoice extraction. The original invoice and Peppol lifecycle message are preserved.\n    - Fixed misleading “not found in Annuaire” errors when a directory lookup fails temporarily.\n    - France e-reporting submission now selects a legal entity using the [legal-entity-scoped submission operation](#tag/France-PPF-Submission/operation/submitFranceEReportingXmlForLegalEntity). Use the ID of an active legal entity that is accessible through your API credentials and matches the XML reporting SIREN. Multiple entities may share that SIREN.\n    - The previous submission endpoint remains callable but is deprecated and removed from this reference. It still requires an unambiguous reporting SIREN. Existing clients can continue sending the same XML request without additional parameters or headers. XML retrieval is unchanged.\n    - Added French PPF extraction mappings for consolidated credit notes (type `262`, reported as `381` with the contract reference and billing-period start), VAT exemptions, delivery fields, line selection and prices. The original customer document is preserved.\n    - Active French `0225` receiving registrations are now kept synchronized with the France Annuaire. When an exact PISTE lookup definitively confirms that the corresponding line is absent, ended, or identifies a different business address, the plugin removes its own Peppol publication and changes the registration to `FAILED` while retaining its historical `activationDate`. A participant that has moved to another SMP is never removed from that SMP's SML registration.\n    - Updating a French `0225` receiving registration now follows its lifecycle state: supported-document changes are published to Peppol once the registration is active. Enabling an existing sender-only registration starts the Annuaire activation workflow; disabling a receiving registration through PUT is rejected and requires DELETE.\n    - Improved documentation\n- 1.21 - September 2026\n    - Fixed an issue that could prevent French invoice status updates from being delivered.\n    - Recovering a failed French invoice status update now preserves later progress while allowing a current update to take effect.\n    - Retrying a failed France CDAR preserves the applicable PPF reporting setting and genuine invoice transport failures while correcting inconsistent invoice statuses. Unreadable retained XML returns a validation error.\n    - PPF closure checks recognize the sent and received copies of the same invoice when both parties use the service.\n    - Requests without the required administrative privileges return HTTP 403.\n    - Added an endpoint for [retrieving the original France e-reporting XML](#tag/France-PPF-Submission/operation/getFranceEReportingSubmission) by the `submissionId`\n    - Added support and documentation for French sender-only legal entities. These registrations use scheme `0225`, `peppolRegistration=true`, and mandatory `FR_CDAR_REGULATED`. `FR_CDAR_NONREGULATED`, MLR and Invoice Response are optional and are not added automatically. Their identifier must start with a 9-digit SIREN followed by an underscore and non-empty text. Internal MLS capabilities are not exposed through the public API.\n- 1.20 - September 2026\n  - Added `claimedByPa` to each result returned when [searching the France Annuaire by SIREN or SIRET](#tag/France-Annuaire/operation/findPeppolIdentifiersBySirenOrSiret). A value of `false` means that the Annuaire record exists but is not routable because no real Plateforme Agréée has claimed it; `true` means that a real PA is assigned. The platform identifier is not exposed.\n  - Corrected the OpenAPI specification to declare the shared `Order` tag only once, allowing strict validators and client generators to process the specification successfully.\n  - Corrected OpenAPI response schemas, examples, date formats, and license metadata so that strict validation and generated-client compilation succeed.\n  - **Generated-client compatibility notice:** the date-schema correction replaced historical date-time types with strings, changing generated SDK types. The historical types are restored by the compatibility correction documented under 1.23; the response timestamp format did not change.\n- 1.19 - August 2026\n  - Added [Factur-X generation from a built-in France CII template](#tag/France-Factur-X-Generation/operation/generateFromTemplate), requiring only the seller and buyer Peppol identifiers and SIRENs, with optional VAT identifiers and an optional human-readable PDF language (`FR`, the default, or `EN`). Generated seller and buyer SIRENs use the French `0002` identifier scheme.\n  - Added [Factur-X generation from a supplied EN16931 CII](#tag/France-Factur-X-Generation/operation/generateFromCii), with an optional readable PDF/A-1 or PDF/A-3 document. When the readable PDF is omitted, it is generated in French by default or in the requested `FR` or `EN` language. Invalid CII responses include the detailed XML, XSD, or Schematron validation report. These generation endpoints return the PDF and do not submit it to Peppol.\n  - Corrected the France PPF submission retrieval contract so generated clients expose the returned `application/xml` response body instead of treating the endpoint as a DTO/no-content response.\n  - Extended structured France CDAR submissions with requested-action code and text, detailed-status sequence numbers, and general document characteristics such as the paired `DIV`/`DVA` VAT-rate correction values from XP Z12-012 Annexe A/B v1.4.\n  - Completed CDAR sending and receiving notifications with root notes, requested actions, amounts, and document characteristics.\n  - Detailed-status sequence numbers are now allocated automatically when omitted, and root CDAR notes preserve their supported content, content-code, and subject-code fields.\n  - Corrected the France CDAR OpenAPI examples to use French motif codes such as `TX_TVA_ERR`; approved status `205` no longer carries the invalid `APP` motif example.\n- 1.18 - August 2026\n  - Added support for embedding Base64 attachments in PA-to-PA CDAR submissions. These attachments are omitted from the PPF-bound CDAR as required by the French PPF profile.\n  - Added support for MEN, RAP, MPA, ESC, RAB, and REM amount details in structured JSON CDAR submissions, including the currency and VAT rate required for the generated CDAR XML.\n  - Creating a French Peppol registration now validates and creates its France Annuaire directory line synchronously, then starts activation; Peppol network activation follows after the line becomes effective. V2 responses expose `PENDING_ACTIVATION` while activation is pending.\n  - Creating a French legal entity with an enabled `0225` Peppol registration uses the same Annuaire workflow; the legal entity is created immediately while the embedded registration remains `PENDING_ACTIVATION` until its directory line is effective.\n  - Deleting a French `0225` Peppol registration removes its Peppol publication and requests closure or cancellation of its France Annuaire line. Deleting the whole legal entity applies the same workflow to every eligible registration. Effective closure of an active line is confirmed asynchronously as described under API 2.0.\n- 1.17 - July 2026\n  - Added [support for France UBL, CII, and Factur-X self-billing invoices and credit notes](#section/Country-Specifics/France-self-billing) identified from their BT-3 document type code\n  - Possibility to search exchanged documents using the legal entity id\n  - Added an endpoint for [retrieving PPF submissions](#tag/France-PPF-Submission/operation/getFranceEInvoicingSubmission) to retrieve the content of the PPF submissions sent to the French authorities.\n  - Added an endpoint for [requesting France PPF C5 reporting](#tag/France-PPF-Submission/operation/requestFranceEInvoicingC5Reporting) for an already sent France e-invoicing document.\n  - Legal entity creation, legal entity updates, and Peppol registration updates now validate that the participant identifier scheme is allowed for the legal entity country; invalid combinations are rejected with a `LEGAL_ENTITY_ERROR`.\n  - Legal entity creation, legal entity updates, and Peppol registration updates now validate that France legal entities support all mandatory France document types; missing document types are rejected with a `LEGAL_ENTITY_ERROR`.\n  - Enhanced C5 notifications to include more details about the C5 submission status and acknowledgements.\n- 1.16 - July 2026\n  - Legal entities can now be deleted even if they have exchanged documents\n  - Added an endpoint for [searching exchanged documents](#tag/Documents/operation/getDocumentsV2), such as invoices and orders, using common document, participant, transmission, country, and direction filters.\n  - Added an endpoint for [searching the France Annuaire by SIREN or SIRET](#tag/France-Annuaire/operation/findPeppolIdentifiersBySirenOrSiret) to retrieve the currently effective Peppol electronic invoicing identifiers.\n- 1.15 - May 2026\n  - Possibility to skip C5 submission on demand\n- 1.14 - May 2026\n  - Possibility to [ submit a CDAR](#tag/France-CDAR/operation/sendCDARV2)\n  - Enhanced support for [CDAR notifications](#tag/Notification/operation/getNotificationsV2)\n  - Support for [France authority e-reporting flow](#tag/France-PPF-Submission/operation/submitFranceEReportingXmlForLegalEntity)\n  - Possibility to [download Factur-X invoices](#tag/InvoiceCredit-Note/operation/getInvoiceInFacturxFormat)\n  - Added a new `DOCUMENT_RECEIVE_FAILED` [notification type](#tag/Notification/operation/getNotificationsV2) for incoming documents that are rejected due to technical issues (e.g., invalid format, failed validation, etc)\n  - Included more details in the `INVOICE_RESPONSE_SENT` and `INVOICE_RESPONSE_RECEIVED` notifications\n  - The legacy Participant API has been removed\n- 1.13 - March 2026\n  - Ability to [Retrieve the transport evidence](#tag/Transport-Evidences/operation/downloadTransportEvidence) for a transmission ID. This can be used to demonstrate that the document was delivered to the receiver Access Point.\n  - Ability to [Retrieve the number of documents exchanged within a specified period](#tag/Statistics/operation/countDocuments).The period and Peppol identifier are optional filters.\n  - Improved validation error messages when a document cannot be delivered to the receiver Access Point due to a technical issue.\n- 1.12 - February 2026\n  - Possibility to retrieve the transport evidences for a sent or received document\n- 1.11 - A typical successful lifecycle is <code>C5_DOCUMENT_ENQUEUED</code> &rarr; <code>C5_DOCUMENT_SUBMITTED</code> &rarr; <code>C5_DOCUMENT_ACKNOWLEDGED</code> &rarr; <code>C5_DOCUMENT_PROCESSED</code>. <code>C5_DOCUMENT_ENQUEUED</code> means that the entry is accepted for reporting and has not yet been sent to PPF. <code>C5_DOCUMENT_SUBMITTED</code> means that the bulk archive containing the entry was uploaded to PPF; it does not confirm technical or business acceptance. <code>C5_DOCUMENT_SUBMISSION_FAILED</code> reports a submission failure, including an upload failure after retries are exhausted. PPF technical acceptance or rejection is reported by <code>C5_DOCUMENT_ACKNOWLEDGED</code> or <code>C5_DOCUMENT_NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED</code>; business processing results are reported by <code>C5_DOCUMENT_PROCESSED</code> or <code>C5_DOCUMENT_PROCESSING_FAILED</code>. <code>C5SendingNotificationROV2</code> reports reporting acceptance and submission outcomes; <code>C5ReceivingNotificationROV2</code> reports PPF technical and business responses. The <code>success</code> field applies only to the stage identified by <code>eventType</code>. <code>submissionId</code> identifies the individual entry, <code>c5TransmissionId</code> the outbound bulk archive, and <code>acknowledgementId</code> the incoming PPF response archive. <code>c5TransmissionId</code> can be absent while the entry is only enqueued. The Peppol <code>transmissionId</code> can be absent for standalone e-reporting. Use <code>details</code> and, when present, <code>documentStatusDetails</code> for rejection reasons.</br></br><b>France CDAR notifications</b></br><code>CDAR_SENT</code> confirms that a France invoice lifecycle CDAR message was sent successfully; <code>CDAR_SEND_FAILED</code> reports that sending the CDAR failed. Both use <code>CDARSendingNotificationROV2</code>. <code>CDAR_RECEIVED</code> uses <code>CDARReceivingNotificationROV2</code> and reports a received CDAR status update for a referenced invoice or credit note. These events concern the lifecycle message itself, including messages generated automatically by the platform. <code>DOCUMENT_SENT</code> and <code>DOCUMENT_RECEIVED</code> concern the original document exchange. In CDAR notifications, <code>currentDocument</code> identifies the CDAR and <code>referencedDocument</code> identifies the invoice or credit note. <code>documentStatus</code> carries the French lifecycle status (for example, <code>FR_DEPOSITED</code> or <code>FR_APPROVED</code>), while <code>detailedStatuses</code> and <code>details</code> provide additional information when available.
